meta.statement:
Let $X$ be a connected compact Kähler manifold, and let $\theta$ be a smooth
closed real $(1,1)$-form such that $\operatorname{PSH}(X,\theta)\ne\varnothing$.
Write

$$
\mathscr D_{\mathcal I}(X,\theta)
:=\operatorname{PSH}(X,\theta)/{\sim_{\mathcal I}}
$$

for the set of *realizable* $\mathcal I$-data. Thus an element is induced by
an actual $\varphi\in\operatorname{PSH}(X,\theta)$ and is represented by the
tower $(\mathcal I(m\varphi))_{m\ge1}$, equivalently by its divisorial Lelong
profile; it is not an arbitrary formal sequence of ideals. For
$d=[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}$, define

$$
\mathcal R_\theta(d):=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}.
$$

**Theorem (P14.8 v5).**

1. The map $\mathcal R_\theta$ is well defined and returns the unique
   normalized $\mathcal I$-model potential in the class $d$. Hence full
   realizable $\mathcal I$-data reconstructs its canonical normalized
   $\mathcal I$-model representative, with no hypothesis on nonpluripolar
   mass.

2. Raw nonpluripolar mass is not part of $\mathcal I$-data. On
   $X=\mathbf P^1$, equipped with the Fubini--Study form $\omega$ normalized
   by $\int_X\omega=1$, there is one $\mathcal I$-class containing potentials
   $\varphi_s$, $0\le s\le1$, such that

   $$
   [\varphi_s]_{\mathcal I}=[0]_{\mathcal I},\qquad
   \int_X\left\langle\omega+\operatorname{dd}^c\varphi_s\right\rangle=1-s.
   $$

   In particular, the raw zero-mass representative $\varphi_1$ has canonical
   normalized $\mathcal I$-model representative $0$, whose mass is one. So
   neither a raw zero-mass representative nor its mass can be reconstructed
   from its $\mathcal I$-class.

These settle the two defined readings of the former P14.8 wording: complete
realizable $\mathcal I$-data determines the canonical normalized
$\mathcal I$-model representative, while neither a raw representative nor
its raw mass descends to the $\mathcal I$-quotient.

**Scope.** On a smooth projective variety, the separate all-mass order
isomorphism for full realized DXZ--Boucksom--Jonsson objects in a
pseudoeffective real Néron--Severi class remains distinct. The literal
all-semivaluation ideal formula is used only for a $\mathbf Q$-line-bundle
class. This theorem asserts neither a compact-Kähler nor a genuinely
transcendental extension of that result. Realization of arbitrary formal
ideal or valuative data remains P14.1, and the P14.7 terminal-left-limit
corollary is not used here.

The exact source excerpts used by the proof are appended to its frozen V6
packet: Boucksom's multiplier-ideal notes, BEGZ's nonpluripolar-product
paper, and Kellay--Mashreghi, arXiv:1102.5596, formula (3.4), for the
generalized-Cantor capacity criterion.

record.location: Proof, first paragraph: closure of \(\mathcal F_d\) under finite maxima
record.detail: A finite maximum of theta-psh functions is theta-psh and remains at most zero. For every prime divisor over X, the generic divisorial Lelong number of max(psi_1,psi_2) is the minimum of the two generic Lelong numbers. Since both inputs have the same divisorial profile d, the maximum has that profile too; the valuative multiplier-ideal criterion at every positive integral scaling then gives the same full ideal tower. Induction gives closure under arbitrary finite maxima.

record.location: Proof, second paragraph: Choquet sequence and preservation of divisorial Lelong numbers
record.detail: Choquet's lemma supplies a countable sequence whose regularized supremum is U. Finite maxima u_j stay in the competitor family and increase almost everywhere to U. For a fixed prime divisor E on a model, a point can be chosen outside the countable union of exceptional analytic subsets for all pullbacks u_j and U, so point and generic Lelong numbers agree simultaneously. After addition of a smooth local potential, the local functions are psh and the increasing-limit theorem applies, with Lelong numbers decreasing to that of the a.e. limit. Every u_j has profile d, hence nu(U,E)=nu(d,E). This is repeated for each E; no single point common to different divisors is required.

record.detail: Equality of all divisorial Lelong numbers for U and a representative of d, followed by the valuative criterion for each positive integral multiple, yields equality of every multiplier ideal in the tower. The quotient is restricted to realizable d, which supplies the initial competitor.

record.location: Proof, end of first-assertion argument: normalization, idempotence, and uniqueness
record.detail: Because U is the largest competitor and belongs to its own class, applying the same envelope to U returns U, giving the I-model fixed-point property. If sup_X U were negative, a sufficiently small positive constant could be added while retaining the bound by zero, theta-psh status, and multiplier ideals, contradicting maximality; hence sup_X U=0. Any normalized I-model potential in d is a fixed point of the identical competitor envelope and therefore equals U. This proves existence and uniqueness without a nonpluripolar-mass hypothesis.

record.location: Proof, generalized Cantor construction
record.detail: With ell_0=1 and ell_m=exp(-4^m), the explicit inequalities 2 ell_1<ell_0 and 2 ell_{m+1}<ell_m allow two children at every stage. Assigning mass 2^{-m} to each stage-m interval is consistent and yields a probability measure supported on the limiting compact set. Any point is contained in at most a bounded number of stage-m intervals, so its mass is bounded by a constant times 2^{-m} and is zero; the limiting measure is nonatomic. The capacity criterion has summands 2^{-m} log(1/ell_m)=2^m, so the series diverges. Rescaling the initial circle length changes the logarithms by a bounded additive constant and does not affect divergence. Hence the compact support F has logarithmic capacity zero and is polar/pluripolar on P^1.

record.location: Proof, construction and integration of the Green potentials
record.detail: For each p on P^1 the normalized Green potential satisfies omega+dd^c G_p=delta_p and sup G_p=0. Integration against the probability measure defines an upper-bounded potential G_mu. At any point outside the compact support F, positive distance from F uniformly bounds the logarithmic kernels below, so G_mu is finite there and is not identically minus infinity. Distributional Fubini gives omega+dd^c G_mu=mu, a positive order-zero current/measure of total mass one supported on F. Thus phi_s=sG_mu is omega-psh and omega+dd^c phi_s=(1-s)omega+s mu for 0<=s<=1.

record.location: Proof, vanishing Lelong numbers and scaled multiplier ideals
record.detail: On a Riemann surface, the Lelong number of the positive (1,1)-current omega+dd^c phi_s at a point is its atomic mass (up to the fixed convention already normalized by the Green equation). Both omega and mu are nonatomic, so every point Lelong number is zero. Birational models of a smooth curve introduce no new divisorial valuations beyond points, so every divisorial Lelong number is zero. Scaling by each positive integer preserves zero, and the valuative multiplier-ideal criterion then puts 1 in I(m phi_s), hence I(m phi_s)=O_X for all m. Therefore every phi_s has the same realizable I-data as 0.

record.location: Proof, BEGZ degree-one nonpluripolar mass computation
record.detail: The Green potential G_mu is locally bounded on X\F. By plurifine locality, on X\F the degree-one nonpluripolar product equals the ordinary positive current (1-s)omega+s mu; since mu is supported on F, its restriction there is (1-s)omega. The nonpluripolar product puts no mass on the pluripolar set F, and the smooth area measure also assigns F zero mass. Consequently the global product is exactly (1-s)omega and, under the normalization integral omega=1, its total mass is 1-s. This is equality of positive measures, so no invalid passage from signed mass to total variation is involved.

results.title: Relative non-pluripolar products of currents
results.theorem:
Let $U$ be an open subset of $\mathbb{C}^{n}$. Let $(u^{l}_{j})_{l}$ be a sequence of psh functions on $U$ and $u_{j}$ a psh function on $U$ for $1\leq j\leq m$. Let $(T_{l})_{l}$ be a sequence of closed positive currents satisfying Condition $(*)$ and $T_{l}$ converges to a closed positive current $T$ on $U$ as $l\to\infty$. Assume that one of the following conditions is satisfied:


$(i)$ $u_{j}^{l}\geq u_{j}$ and $u_{j}^{l}$ converges to $u_{j}$ in $L^{1}_{loc}$ as $l\to\infty$.


$(ii)$ $u_{j}^{l}$ increases to $u_{j}$ as $l\to\infty$ almost everywhere and $T$ has no mass on pluripolar sets.


Then, for every smooth weakly positive form $\Phi$ with compact support in $U$, we have



$\liminf_{l\to\infty}\int_{U}\langle\wedge_{j=1}^{m}dd^{c}u_{j}^{l}\dot{\wedge}T_{l}\rangle\wedge\Phi\geq\int_{U}\langle\wedge_{j=1}^{m}dd^{c}u_{j}\dot{\wedge}T\rangle\wedge\Phi.$

results.title: The Levi Problem in $\mathbb C^n$: A Survey
results.theorem:
Let $U\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ be open and $f_{j}\colon U\to[-\infty,\infty)$ a non-increasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions which converges
pointwise to $f\colon U\to[-\infty,\infty)$. Then $f$ is plurisubharmonic.

results.title: Viscosity solutions to quaternionic Monge-Ampère equations
results.theorem:
(1) (Theorem 3.1 in [22]) Let $v^{1},\ldots,v^{n}\in PSH\cap L_{loc}^{\infty}(\Omega)$. Let $\{v_{j}^{1}\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}},\ldots,\{v_{j}^{n}\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ be decreasing sequences of $PSH$ functions in $\Omega$ such that $\lim_{j\rightarrow\infty}v_{j}^{t}=v^{t}$ pointwisely in $\Omega$ for each $t$. Then the currents $\triangle v_{j}^{1}\wedge\ldots\wedge\triangle v_{j}^{n}$ converge weakly to $\triangle v^{1}\wedge\ldots\wedge\triangle v^{n}$ as $j\rightarrow\infty$.
(2) (Proposition 4.1 in [23]) Let $\{u_{j}\}_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $PSH\cap L_{loc}^{\infty}(\Omega)$ that increases to $u\in PSH\cap L_{loc}^{\infty}(\Omega)$ almost everywhere in $\Omega$ $($with respect to Lebesgue measure$)$. Then the currents $(\triangle u_{j})^{n}$ converge weakly to $(\triangle u)^{n}$ as $j\rightarrow\infty$.

results.title: Weak convergence of Monge-Ampère measures on compact Hermitian manifolds
results.theorem: Let $\{u_{j}\}$ be a uniformly bounded sequence of $\omega$-psh functions. Assume $(\omega+dd^{c}u_{j})^{n}\leq C(\omega+dd^{c}\varphi_{j})^{n}$ for some uniformly bounded sequence $\{\varphi_{j}\}$ such that $\varphi_{j}\to\varphi\in PSH(X,\omega)$ in capacity. If $u_{j}\to u\in PSH(X,\omega)\cap L^{\infty}(X)$ in $L^{1}(X)$, then a subsequence of $(\omega+dd^{c}u_{j})^{n}$ converges weakly to $(\omega+dd^{c}u)^{n}$.

results.title: Plurifinely Plurisubharmonic functions and the Monge Ampère Operator
results.theorem:
Let $\Omega$ be open in
${{\mathbb{C}}}^{n}$, $n\geq 1$, let ${\mathcal{O}}\subset\Omega$ be a plurifine open subset, and let
$(u_{j}^{1})$ and $(u_{j}^{2})$ be two monotone sequences of plurisubharmonic
functions that are bounded in $\Omega$, each converging to a bounded plurisubharmonic
function $u^{1}$, respectively $u^{2}$ on $\Omega$.
If $(dd^{c}(u_{j}^{1}-u_{j}^{2}))^{n}|_{\mathcal{O}}\geq 0$, then
$(dd^{c}(u_{1}-u_{2}))^{n}|_{\mathcal{O}}\geq 0$.

results.title: Hardy and Bergman spaces on hyperconvex domains and their composition operators
results.theorem:
Suppose that $u$ is a plurisubharmonic function,
the set $L(u)$ is compact and $T$ is a closed positive current of
bidegree $(1,1)$, then the current $(dd^{c}u)^{n-1}\wedge T$ is well
defined and has locally finite mass on $D$. Moreover, if $\{u_{k}\}$
is a sequence of decreasing plurisubharmonic functions converging
to $u$, then the currents $(dd^{c}u_{k})^{n-1}\wedge T$ converge
weak-$*$ to $(dd^{c}u)^{n-1}\wedge T$.

results.title: On the weighted m-energy classes
results.theorem:
Let $\chi:\mathbb{R}^{-}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{-}$ be an increasing function such that $\chi(-t)<0$ for every $t>0$, and $u\in\mathcal{N}_{m}(\Omega)$. Suppose that



$\int\limits_{\Omega}(-\chi\circ u)(dd^{c}u)^{m}\wedge\omega^{n-m}<+\infty.$



Then there exists a sequence $\{u_{j}\}\in\mathcal{E}_{0,m}(\Omega)$ such that $u_{j}\searrow u$ and



$\lim\limits_{j\rightarrow\infty}\int\limits_{\Omega}(-\chi\circ u_{j})(dd^{c}u_{j})^{m}\wedge\omega^{n-m}=\int\limits_{\Omega}(-\chi\circ u)(dd^{c}u)^{m}\wedge\omega^{n-m}.$

results.title: Approximation of maximal plurisubharmonic functions
results.theorem:
Let $u_{0},...,u_{q}$ be locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions in a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ ($0\leq q\leq n$)
and let $u_{0}^{k},...,u_{q}^{k}$ be decreasing sequences of plurisubharmonic functions converging pointwise to $u_{0},...,u_{q}$. Let $T$ be
a closed, positive current of bidegree $(n-q,n-q)$ in $\Omega$. Then
$u_{0}^{k}dd^{c}u_{1}^{k}\wedge...\wedge dd^{c}u_{q}^{k}\wedge T$ converges weakly to $u_{0}dd^{c}u_{1}\wedge...\wedge dd^{c}u_{q}\wedge T.$

results.title: Quantitative stability for the complex Monge-Ampere equations
results.theorem:
Let $\Omega$ be an open subset in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$. Let $(u_{j})_{j}$ be a sequence of psh functions converging to a psh function $u_{\infty}$ in capacity in $\Omega$. Assume that the non-pluripolar product $(dd^{c}u_{j})^{n}$ is well-defined for $1\leq j\leq\infty$, and there exists a non-pluripolar Radon measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ such that $(dd^{c}u_{j})^{n}\leq\mu$ for every $j$. Then $(dd^{c}u_{j})^{n}$ converges
weakly to $(dd^{c}u_{\infty})^{n}$ as $j\to\infty$.

results.title: Polynomials associated to non-convex bodies
results.theorem:
Let $\{\psi_{n}\}$ be a locally uniformly bounded above family of plurisubharmonic functions on $\mathbb{C}^{d}$. Suppose for any subsequence $J$ of positive integers we have



$\bigl{(}\limsup_{n\in J}\psi_{n}(z)\bigr{)}^{*}=V(z)$



for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^{d}$ where $V\in PSH(\mathbb{C}^{d})\cap L^{\infty}_{loc}(\mathbb{C}^{d})$. Then $\psi_{n}\to V$ in $L_{loc}^{1}(\mathbb{C}^{d})$.

results.title: On the multipoled global Zhou weights and semi-continuity for Zhou numbers
results.theorem:
Let $\varphi$ be a plurisubharmonic function on a complex manifold $X$. Then, for every $c>0$, the Lelong number upper-level set

results.title: Hybrid convergence of Kähler-Einstein measures
results.theorem:
Let $\Omega$ be a semi-positive $(1,1)$-current on a smooth complex manifold $Z$, $D$ be a smooth prime divisor on $Z$, and $p$ a point of $D$.

If $z$ a local equation for $D$ at $p$, and $\phi$ a local potential near $p$ such that $\Omega=dd^{c}\phi$, then the Lelong number $\nu_{D}(\Omega,p)$ of $\Omega$ along $D$ is defined by the following formula:



$\nu_{D}(\Omega,p)=\max\{a>0/\phi-a\log\lvert z\rvert\;\emph{is bounded from above}\}.$

results.title: Injectivity theorem for pseudo-effective line bundles and its applications
results.theorem:
Let $F$ be a holomorphic line bundle on a complex manifold $X$ and
let $h$ be a singular Hermitian metric on $F$.
We assume $\sqrt{-1}\Theta_{h}(F)\geq\gamma$
for some smooth $(1,1)$-form $\gamma$ on $X$.
We fix a smooth Hermitian metric $h_{\infty}$ on $F$.
Then we can write $h=h_{\infty}e^{-2\psi}$ for some
$\psi\in L^{1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(X)$.
Then
$\psi$ coincides with a quasi-plurisubharmonic
function $\varphi$ on $X$ almost everywhere.
We define the multiplier ideal sheaf
$\mathcal{J}(h)$ of $h$ by $\mathcal{J}(h):=\mathcal{J}(\varphi)$.

results.title: On equisingular approximation of plurisubharmonic functions
results.theorem:
Let $\varphi$ be a psh function defined on a complex manifold $X$. The multiplier ideal sheaf $\mathcal{J}(\varphi)$ of $\varphi$ is the ideal sheaf of the sheaf of holomorphic functions on $X$ whose germ at each $x\in X$ is equal to



$\left\{f\in\mathcal{O}_{x}:{\lvert f\rvert}^{2}e^{-2\varphi}\ \text{is integrable with respect to the Lebesgue measure near}\ x\right\}.$

results.title: The exactness of a general Skoda complex
results.theorem:
Let $\mathcal{J}(\psi)$ be the multiplier ideal sheaf of a plurisubharmonic function $\psi$ which is defined in a neighborhood of $x$. There exists an integer $p^{\prime}\geq p$ such that for every $0\leq r\leq p$, the natural map





$H_{r}\left(K_{\bullet}(h_{1},\cdots,h_{p})\otimes\mathfrak{a}^{p^{\prime}-r}\mathcal{J}(\psi)\right)\rightarrow H_{r}\left(K_{\bullet}(h_{1},\cdots,h_{p})\otimes\mathcal{J}(\psi)\right)$



vanishes.

results.title: A non-Archimedean Ohsawa-Takegoshi extension theorem
results.theorem:
Let $\varphi$ be a quasisubharmonic function on $X$ with $\varphi\leq 0$.
For any $x\in X$, the local multiplier ideal of $\varphi$ at $x$, denoted $\mathcal{J}(\varphi)_{x}$, consists of those germs $f\in\mathcal{O}_{X,x}$ such that for all $\epsilon>0$, there is an affinoid neighborhood $V_{\epsilon}$ of $x$ on which $f$ is defined such that



$\sup_{V_{\epsilon}\backslash Z(\varphi)}|f|e^{-(1+\epsilon)\varphi-A}<+\infty.$

results.title: Multiplier ideals of monomial space curves
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a smooth irreducible variety over $\mathbb{C}$. Let $I\subseteq\mathcal{O}_{X}$ be a nonzero ideal sheaf and let $\lambda>0$ be a rational number. Fix a log resolution $\mu:\widetilde{X}\to X$ of $I$ and let $F$ be the effective divisor such that $I\cdot\mathcal{O}_{X}=\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}}(-F)$. The multiplier ideal $\mathcal{J}(I^{\lambda})\subseteq\mathcal{O}_{X}$ associated to $\lambda$ and $I$ is defined to be



$\mathcal{J}(I^{\lambda})=\mu_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{X}}(K_{\widetilde{X}/X}-\lfloor\lambda\cdot F\rfloor).$

results.title: Global pluripotential theory on hybrid spaces
results.theorem:
Let $\mathscr{J}\subset\mathcal{O}_{Y}$ be a coherent ideal sheaf on $Y$, and $\phi\in\operatorname{PSH}(Y,L)$. We say that $\phi$ has analytic singularities along $\mathscr{J}$ if $\phi$ can be written locally as:



$\phi=\log\big{(}\lvert f_{1}\rvert^{2}+...+\lvert f_{r}\rvert^{2}\big{)}+\chi,$



where $(f_{1},...,f_{r})$ is a family of local generators of $\mathscr{J}$ and $\chi$ is a smooth function.

results.title: A note on multiplier ideal sheaves on complex spaces with singularities
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a complex space of pure dimension $n$ and $\varphi\in L_{\text{loc}}^{1}(X_{\text{reg}})$ with respect to the Lebesgue measure. Let $X\hookrightarrow\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^{n+r}$ be a local embedding such that $\mathscr{I}_{X}$ is generated by holomorphic functions $g_{1},\dots,g_{m}$ on $\Omega$.


The Nadel-Ohsawa multiplier ideal sheaf $\widehat{\mathscr{I}}(\varphi)$ on $X$ is defined to be the fractional ideal sheaf of germs of meromorphic functions $f\in\mathscr{M}_{X,x}$ such that $|f|^{2}e^{-2\varphi}$ is locally integrable at $x$ on $X$ with respect to the measure $dV_{X}[\Psi]$, where $\Psi=r\log(|g_{1}|^{2}+\cdots+|g_{m}|^{2})$. One can check that $\widehat{\mathscr{I}}(\varphi)$ is independent of the local embedding of $X$ and the choice of generators of $\mathscr{I}_{X}$.

results.title: Equivalence of plurisubharmonic singularities and Siu-type metrics
results.theorem:
Let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be two plurisubharmonic functions on a complex manifold $X$. Suppose that $\psi$ has zero
Lelong number at every point of $X$. Then we have $\mathcal{J}(m(\varphi+\psi))=\mathcal{J}(m\varphi)$ for every real $m>0$.

results.title: Milnor Fiber Consistency via Flatness
results.theorem:
Let $u\geq 0$ be an integer, $X^{\prime}$ a complex-analytic manifold, $X\subseteq X^{\prime}\times\mathbb{C}^{u}$ an open subset, $\pi:X\to\mathbb{C}^{u}$ the restriction to $X$ of the projection onto $\mathbb{C}^{u}$, and $F:X\to\mathbb{C}$ a holomorphic function which is not constant on any connected component of a fiber of $\pi$. Denote by $C_{F\times\pi}$ the vanishing locus of the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{J}_{F\times\pi}$ of maximal minors of the Jacobian matrix of $F\times\pi$.


Then there exists a complex-analytic Whitney stratification of $X$ such that $X\setminus C_{F\times\pi}$ is the ambient stratum, the non-flat locus of the normal cone $C_{C_{F\times\pi}}X$ to $C_{F\times\pi}$ in $X$ over $\mathbb{C}^{u}$ is a union of strata, and the Thom ($a_{F\times\pi}$) condition with respect to the ambient stratum is satisfied on any stratum not contained in this non-flat locus.

results.title: A characterization of multiplier ideals via ultraproducts
results.theorem:
Assume that $X$ is a normal variety over $\mathbb{C}$, $\Delta$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-Weil divisor such that $K_{X}+\Delta$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor, $\mathfrak{a}$ is a non-zero ideal sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ and $t$ is a positive real number. Take a log resolution $\mu:Y\to X$ of $\mathfrak{a}$ such that $\mathfrak{a}\mathcal{O}_{Y}=\mathcal{O}_{Y}(-Z)$. Then the multiplier ideal $\mathcal{J}((X,\Delta),\mathfrak{a}^{t})$ of $((X,\Delta),\mathfrak{a}^{t})$ is defined by



$\mathcal{J}((X,\Delta),\mathfrak{a}^{t})=\mu_{*}\mathcal{O}_{Y}(\lceil K_{Y}-\mu^{*}(K_{X}+\Delta)-tZ\rceil).$

(59)

results.title: Density and intersection of (1,1)-currents
results.theorem:
Let $T_{1},\cdots,T_{m}$ be positive closed $(1,1)-$currents with analytic singularities on a complex manifold $X$ whose supports have compact intersection. Denote by $Z_{j}$ the singular locus of $T_{j}$ and let $Z=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}Z_{j}$. Then the non-pluripolar product $\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle$ is well-defined $X$ and



$\pi^{*}\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle=\mathbf{1}_{\pi^{-1}(X\setminus Z)}S,$



for any density current $S$ associated with $(T_{1},\ldots,T_{m})$.

results.title: Plurisubharmonic envelopes and supersolutions
results.theorem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$ and $\theta$ be a closed smooth semipositive $(1,1)$-form on $X$ such that $\int_{X}\theta^{n}>0$. Let $E\subset X$ be a closed subset of $X$ that has zero Lebesgue measure. If the function $u=-{\bf 1}_{E}$ satisfies



$(\theta+dd^{c}u)^{n}\leq C\omega^{n}$



in the viscosity sense on $X$, then $E$ is pluripolar.

results.title: Unique Ergodicity for foliations on compact Kähler surfaces
results.theorem:
Let $T$ be a positive ${dd^{c}}$-closed $(1,1)$-current of a compact Kähler surface $X$. Assume that the set $\{\nu(T,\cdot)>0\}$ is of Hausdorff $2$-dimensional measure $0$.
Then the cohomology class $\{T\}$ of $T$ is nef, and when $T$ is not closed, $\{T\}$ is also big. In particular, if $T$ is a positive closed $(1,1)$-current having no mass on proper analytic subsets of $X$, then $\{T\}$ is nef.

results.title: Density and intersection of (1,1)-currents
results.theorem:
Let $T_{1},\ldots,T_{m}$ be positive closed $(1,1)-$currents with analytic singularities whose supports have compact intersection. Denote by $Z_{j}$ the singular locus of $T_{j}$ and let $Z=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}Z_{j}$. Then the non-pluripolar product $\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle$ is well-defined and every density current $S$ associated with $(T_{1},\ldots,T_{m})$ satisfies



$\mathbf{1}_{\pi^{-1}(X\setminus Z)}S=\pi^{*}\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle.$



In particular $\pi^{*}\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle\leq S$ and if the Dinh-Sibony product of $T_{1},\ldots,T_{m}$ is well defined we have $\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle\leq T_{1}\curlywedge\cdots\curlywedge T_{m}$.

$\operatorname{codim}A_{j_{1}}\cap\dots\cap A_{j_{m}}\geqslant m,$



alors les courants $u_{1}(dd^{c}u_{2})\wedge\dots\wedge(dd^{c}u_{q})$ et $(dd^{c}u_{1})\wedge\dots\wedge(dd^{c}u_{q})$ sont bien définis et vérifient les

results.title: Equidistribution for non-pluripolar currents on compact Kähler manifolds
results.theorem:
If $u_{1},\cdots,u_{s}$ are psh functions on the complex manifold $X$, we shall say that the non-pluripolar product $\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle$ is well defined on $X$ if for each compact subset $K$ of $X$, we have



$\displaystyle\sup_{k}\int_{K\cap O_{k}}\omega^{n-s}\wedge\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}\max\{u_{j},-k\}<\infty.$



Then, the non-pluripolar product $\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle$ is defined to be a current satisfying the following:


1.

$\mathbf{1}_{O_{k}}\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle=\mathbf{1}_{O_{k}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}\max\{u_{j},-k\}$;



2.

the current $\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{s}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle$ has no mass on the pluripolar set



$X\setminus\bigcup_{k=1}^{\infty}O_{k}=\{u=-\infty\}.$

It is easy to see that $O_{k}:=\{\varphi>\rho-k\}$ is a plurifine open subset, and for any compact subset $K$ of $X$,



$\displaystyle\sup_{k}\int_{K\cap O_{k}}(\beta+dd^{c}\varphi^{(k)})^{n}$
$\displaystyle\leq\sup_{k}\int_{X}(\beta+dd^{c}\varphi^{(k)})^{n}$





$\displaystyle=\int_{X}\beta^{n}<+\infty.$



Thus the Definition 2.1 of non-pluripolar product is well defined due to [BEGZ10, Definition 1.1], has basic properties in [BEGZ10, Proposition 1.4].

results.title: Monge-Ampère equations in big cohomology classes
results.theorem: Let $T_{1},...,T_{p}$ be closed positive $(1,1)$-currents on a complex manifold $X$ whose non-pluripolar product is well-defined. Then the positive $(p,p)$-current $\langle T_{1}\wedge...\wedge T_{p}\rangle$ is closed.

results.title: On a vanishing theorem due to Bogomolov
results.theorem:
For $j=1,\cdots,p$, let $T_{j}$ and $T^{\prime}_{j}$ be two closed positive $(1,1)$-currents with small unbounded locus (i.e. there exists a (locally) complete pluripolar closed subset $A$ of $X$ outside which the potential is locally bounded) in the same cohomology class, and assume also that $T_{j}$ is less singular than $T^{\prime}_{j}$. Then the cohomology classes of their non-pluripolar products satisfy
$\{\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{p}\rangle\}\geq\{\langle T^{\prime}_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T^{\prime}_{p}\rangle\}$
in $H^{p,p}(X,\mathbb{R})$, where $\geq$ means that the difference is pseudo-effective, i.e. representable by a closed positive $(p,p)$-current.

results.title: Dynamics in several complex variables: endomorphisms of projective spaces and polynomial-like mapping
results.theorem:
Let $u_{1},\ldots,u_{p}$, $p\leq k$, be locally bounded p.s.h. functions on
$X$. Then, the current ${dd^{c}}u_{1}\wedge\ldots\wedge{dd^{c}}u_{p}$
has no mass on locally pluripolar sets, in particular on
proper analytic sets of $X$.

results.title: Dynamical properties of families of holomorphic mapping
results.theorem: Let $u_{1},\ldots,u_{p}$, $p\leq k$, be locally bounded p.s.h. functions on $X$. Then the current $dd^{c}u_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^{c}u_{q}$ has no mass on locally pluripolar sets, in particular, on proper analytic sets of $X$.

results.title: On a vanishing theorem due to Bogomolov
results.theorem:
For $j=1,\cdots,p$, let $T_{j}$ and $T^{\prime}_{j}$ be two closed positive $(1,1)$-currents with small unbounded locus (i.e. there exists a (locally) complete pluripolar closed subset $A$ of $X$ outside which the potential is locally bounded) in the same cohomology class, and assume also that $T_{j}$ is less singular than $T^{\prime}_{j}$. Then the cohomology classes of their non-pluripolar products satisfy
$\{\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{p}\rangle\}\geq\{\langle T^{\prime}_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T^{\prime}_{p}\rangle\}$
in $H^{p,p}(X,\mathbb{R})$, where $\geq$ means that the difference is pseudo-effective, i.e. representable by a closed positive $(p,p)$-current.

results.title: Integration by parts formula for non-pluripolar product
results.theorem:
Let $\varphi_{1},\ldots,\varphi_{p}\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta)$ ($p\leq n$) be potentials with small unbounded loci. Let $A\subseteq X$ be a closed pluripolar set, such that $\varphi_{j}\in L^{\infty}_{\operatorname{loc}}(X-A)$ for $j=1,\ldots,p$. Then



$\theta_{\varphi_{1}}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_{p}}=\mathds{1}_{X-A}\,\theta_{\varphi_{1}|_{X-A}}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_{p}|_{X-A}}.$



On RHS, the product is the usual Bedford–Taylor product ([BT82]) on $X-A$, $\mathds{1}_{X-A}$ formally denotes the zero-extension to $X$.

results.title: Density and intersection of (1,1)-currents
results.theorem:
Let $T_{1},\cdots,T_{m}$ be positive closed $(1,1)-$currents with analytic singularities on a complex manifold $X$ whose supports have compact intersection. Denote by $Z_{j}$ the singular locus of $T_{j}$ and let $Z=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}Z_{j}$. Then the non-pluripolar product $\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle$ is well-defined $X$ and



$\pi^{*}\langle T_{1}\wedge\cdots\wedge T_{m}\rangle=\mathbf{1}_{\pi^{-1}(X\setminus Z)}S,$



for any density current $S$ associated with $(T_{1},\ldots,T_{m})$.

results.title: Chern forms of hermitian metrics with analytic singularities on vector bundles
results.theorem:
Let $u_{1},\ldots,u_{m}$ be psh functions on a complex manifold $X$ such that the
unbounded locus $L(u_{j})$ is contained in analytic set $Z_{j}\subset X$ for
each $j$. Moreover, let $T$ be a closed positive current of
bidegree $(p,p)$ with support contained in an analytic set $W\subset X$.
Assume that



${\rm codim\,}(Z_{i_{1}}\cap\cdots\cap Z_{i_{\ell}}\cap W)\geq\ell+p$



for all choices of $1\leq i_{1}<\cdots<i_{\ell}\leq m$.
Then
$u_{m}dd^{c}u_{m-1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^{c}u_{1}\wedge T$ and
$dd^{c}u_{m}\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^{c}u_{1}\wedge T$ are well-defined and
have locally finite mass. The latter is a closed positive current.

results.title: Convergence of the weak Kähler-Ricci Flow on manifolds of general type
results.theorem:
If $u_{1},\ldots,u_{p}$ are psh functions on $X$, we say that the non-pluripolar product $\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^{p}dd^{c}u_{j}\rangle$ is well-defined on $X$ if for each compact subset $K$ of $X$ we have



$\sup_{k}\int_{K\cap O_{k}}\omega^{n-p}\cap\bigwedge dd^{c}\max\{u_{j},-k\}<\infty.$

(1.1)

results.title: Géométrie d'Arakelov des variétés toriques et fibrés en droites intégrables
results.theorem:
Soient $u_{1},\dots,u_{q}$ plurisousharmoniques sur $U$ et telles que pour tout $1\leqslant i\leqslant q$, $L(u_{i})$ est contenu dans un ensemble analytique $A_{i}\subset U$. Si pour tout choix d’indices $j_{1}<\dots j_{m}$ dans $\{1,\dots,q\}$, on a :



$\operatorname{codim}A_{j_{1}}\cap\dots\cap A_{j_{m}}\geqslant m,$



alors les courants $u_{1}(dd^{c}u_{2})\wedge\dots\wedge(dd^{c}u_{q})$ et $(dd^{c}u_{1})\wedge\dots\wedge(dd^{c}u_{q})$ sont bien définis et vérifient les
propriétés d’approximation énoncées au théorème (4.2.9).

results.title: Monge-Ampère measures on contact sets
results.theorem:
Let $\theta^{1},\ldots,\theta^{n}$ be smooth closed real $(1,1)$-forms on $X$ such that the cohomology classes
$\{\theta^{1}\},\ldots,\{\theta^{n}\}$ are pseudoeffectives. For $1\leq i\leq n$, let $\varphi_{i}$ be a $\theta^{i}$-psh function and $f_{i}$ be a $C^{1,\bar{1}}$ function on $X$ such that $\varphi_{i}\leq f_{i}$. Then the non-pluripolar product
$\theta^{1}_{\varphi_{1}}\wedge\ldots\wedge\theta^{n}_{\varphi_{n}}$ satisfies the equality:





${\bf 1}_{\bigcap_{j}\{\varphi_{j}=f_{j}\}}\theta^{1}_{\varphi_{1}}\wedge\ldots\wedge\theta^{n}_{\varphi_{n}}={\bf 1}_{\bigcap_{j}\{\varphi_{j}=f_{j}\}}\theta^{1}_{f_{1}}\wedge\ldots\wedge\theta^{n}_{f_{n}}$

(7)

results.title: Dynamics in several complex variables: endomorphisms of projective spaces and polynomial-like mapping
results.theorem:
Let $S$ be a positive closed $(p,p)$-current on $X$ and $u$ a
p.s.h. function on $X$. Assume that $S$ is locally moderate
and $u$ is Hölder continuous. Then the current ${dd^{c}}u\wedge S$ is
locally moderate. In particular, wedge-products of positive closed
$(1,1)$-currents with Hölder continuous local potentials are locally
moderate.

results.title: Null-controllability for weakly dissipative heat-like equations
results.theorem:
Let $(\tau_{n})_{n}\in(0,1)^{\mathbb{N}}$. Assume that $\sum_{n}\tau_{n}<+\infty$. Let $K$ be the associated Smith-Volterra-Cantor set and $\omega\coloneqq{\mathbb{R}}\setminus K$. There exist $c>0$, $C>0$ and $r_{0}>0$ such that for every $0<r<r_{0}$,



$\frac{1}{24}\ \sum_{\rule{0.0pt}{5.12358pt}\mathclap{k\geq\log_{2}(3\operatorname{Leb}(K)/r)}}\ \tau_{k}\leq\inf_{x\in{\mathbb{R}}}\dfrac{\operatorname{Leb}(\omega\cap B(x,r))}{\operatorname{Leb}(B(x,r))}\leq 6\ \sum_{\mathclap{\quad k\geq\log_{2}(\operatorname{Leb}(K)/4r)}}\ \tau_{k},$



where $\log_{2}$ is the base $2$ logarithm $\log_{2}(x)=\ln(x)/\ln(2)$.

results.title: On Fabry's Gap Theorem
results.theorem:
Suppose that $f(z)=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}a_{k}z^{k}$ is a power series with radius of
convergence 1. Assume that there is a subsequence $k_{l}$ of indices, such that
$\limsup\sqrt[k_{l}]{a_{k_{l}}}=1$, and a constant $\theta>0$, such that the
following holds true: If $N_{l}$ denotes the number of indices $k$ within the
interval $[(1-\theta)k_{l},(1+\theta)k_{l}]$, such that $a_{k}\neq 0$, then
$N_{l}/k_{l}\rightarrow 0$. Then the circle $|z|=1$ is the natural boundary of $f$.

results.title: Limit theorems for sums of products of consecutive partial quotients of continued fractions
results.theorem:
Let $\Phi:\mathbb{N}\to[1,\infty)$ be a function with $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Phi(n)=\infty$.
Then the Lebesgue measure of $G(\Phi)$
is either zero or full according as the series ${\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}}\log\Phi(n)/\Phi(n)$ converges or diverges respectively.

results.title: The closed span of some Exponential system $E_{\Lambda}$ in the spaces $L^p(\gamma,\beta)$, properties of a Biorthogonal family to $E_{\Lambda}$ in $L^2(\gamma,\beta)$, Moment problems, and a differential equation of Carleson
results.theorem:
Consider a sequence $\Lambda=\{\lambda_{n}\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of distinct non-zero complex numbers such that
$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}1/|\lambda_{n}|<\infty$ and $\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}|\arg\lambda_{n}|<\pi/2$.
Then its condensation index $c(\Lambda)$ is equal to zero if and only if $\Lambda$ is an interpolating variety for the space $A^{0}_{|z|}$.

results.title: Sobolev spaces, fine gradients and quasicontinuity on quasiopen sets
results.theorem:
Let $x\in X$ and let $\{x_{k}\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of points in $X$
such that $d(x_{k},x)<2^{-k-2}$ for $k=1,2,\dots$ .
If $B_{k}=B(x_{k},3\cdot 2^{-k-2})$,
then a set $E\subset X$ is thin at $x$ if and only if



$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\biggl{(}\frac{\operatorname{cap}_{p}(E\cap B_{k},2B_{k})}{\operatorname{cap}_{p}(B_{k},2B_{k})}\biggr{)}^{1/(p-1)}<\infty.$

results.title: On randomly placed arcs on the circle
results.theorem:
Let $\ell=(\ell_{n})_{n\geq 1}$ be a nonincreasing sequence of positive reals converging to zero and let $g$ be a gauge function. Then, almost surely, for any nonempty open subset $V$ of $\mathbb{T}$,



$E_{\ell}\in\mathrm{G}^{g}(V)\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad\sum\nolimits_{n}g(\ell_{n})=\infty.$

results.title: Logarithm laws for equilibrium states in negative curvature
results.theorem:
Let $(Z,
u)$ be a measured space with finite nonzero measure. Let
$(A_{n})_{n\in{\mathbb{N}}}$ be a sequence of measurable subsets of $Z$ such that
there exists $c>0$ with $
u(A_{n}\cap A_{m})\leq c\;
u(A_{n})\,
u(A_{m})$
for all distinct $n,m$ in ${\mathbb{N}}$. Then $
u(\limsup_{n}A_{n})>0$
if and only if the series $\sum_{n\in{\mathbb{N}}}
u(A_{n})$ diverges.

results.title: Singularity results for functional equations driven by linear fractional transformations
results.theorem:
$(1)$ Suppose that $\limsup_{n\to+\infty}(-\log R_{n})/n\leq\theta_{1}$ for a constant $\theta_{1}$,
then there exists a Borel set $K_{0}$ such that $\mu_{f}(K_{0})=1$ and $\dim_{H}(K_{0})\leq\theta_{1}/\log 2$.
$(2)$ Suppose that $\liminf_{n\to+\infty}(-\log R_{n})/n\geq\theta_{2}$ for a constant $\theta_{2}$,
then we have that $\mu_{f}(K)=0$ for any Borel set $K$ with $\dim_{H}(K)<\theta_{2}/\log 2$.

results.title: Growth of Solutions of Second Order Linear Differential Equations
results.theorem:
Let $f(z)$ be an entire function satisfying $T(r,f)\sim\log M(r,f)$ in a set $E$ of positive upper logarithmic density. For given $0<c<\frac{1}{4}$ and $r\in E$, the set



$I_{r}=\{\theta\in[0,2\pi):\log|f(re^{\iota\theta})|\leq(1-c)\log M(r,f)\}$



has linear measure zero.

results.title: On randomly placed arcs on the circle
results.theorem:
Let $\ell=(\ell_{n})_{n\geq 1}$ be a nonincreasing sequence of positive reals converging to zero and let $g$ be a gauge function. Then, with probability one, for any open subset $V$ of $\mathbb{T}$,



$\mathcal{H}^{g}(E_{\ell}\cap V)=\begin{cases}\mathcal{H}^{g}(V)&\text{if }\sum_{n}g(\ell_{n})=\infty\\[2.84526pt]
0&\text{if }\sum_{n}g(\ell_{n})<\infty.\end{cases}$

results.title: Kähler-Einstein metrics on stable varieties and log canonical pairs
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, $dV$ some volume form, $D=\sum a_{i}D_{i}$ a $\mathbb{R}$-divisor with coefficients in $(-\infty,1]$ and defining sections $s_{i}$, $E=\sum c_{\alpha}E_{\alpha}$ an effective $\mathbb{R}$-divisor such that $D_{red}+E$ has snc support, and $\theta$ a semipositive form with $\int_{X}\theta^{n}>0$ such that $\{\theta\}-c_{1}(E)$ is a Kähler class. Then the $\theta$-psh function $\varphi$ with full Monge-Ampère mass, which is a solution of



$\langle(\theta+dd^{c}\phi)^{n}\rangle=\frac{e^{\varphi}dV}{\prod_{i}|s_{i}|^{2a_{j}}}$



is smooth outside of $\mathrm{Supp}(D)\cup\mathrm{Supp}(E)$.

results.title: A viscosity approach to degenerate complex Monge-Ampère equations
results.theorem:
Let $\omega\geq 0$ be a smooth closed semi-positive $(1,1)-$form on $X$ such that $\int_{X}\omega^{n}>0$ and $\mu=f\mu_{0}$ a volume form on $X$ with density $0\leq f\in L^{p}(X)$ ($p>1$) with respect to a smooth non degenerate volume form $\mu_{0}>0$ such that $\int_{X}\mu=\int_{X}\omega^{n}$. Then there is a unique $\varphi\in PSH(X,\omega)\cap L^{\infty}(X)$ which satisfies the complex Monge-Ampère equation



$(\omega+dd^{c}\varphi)^{n}=f\mu_{0},$



in the pluripotential sense and normalized by $\int_{X}\varphi\mu=0$.

results.title: Continuity of Plurisubharmonic Envelopes in Non-Archimedean Geometry and Test Ideals (with an Appendix by José Ignacio Burgos Gil and Martín Sombra)
results.theorem:
Under the assumptions (A1)–(A3), let $\theta$ be a closed $(1,1)$-form on ${X^{{\mathrm{an}}}}$ with ample de Rham class $\{\theta\}$ and
let $\mu$ be a positive Radon measure on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ of mass $\{\theta\}^{n}$ supported on the skeleton of a projective SNC-model.
Then there is a continuous $\theta$-psh function $\varphi$ on ${X^{{\mathrm{an}}}}$
such that ${\rm MA}_{\theta}(\varphi)=\mu$ and $\varphi$ is unique up to additive constants.

results.title: Strict positivity of Kähler-Einstein currents
results.theorem:
Let $X$ be a Stein space of dimension $n\geqslant 1$, reduced and locally irreducible,
with an isolated log terminal singularity $X_{\rm sing}=\{p\}$.
Let $\Omega\subset X$ be a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain with smooth boundary.
Fix a smooth volume form $dV$ on $X$, $\phi\in{\mathcal{C}}^{\infty}(\partial\Omega)$
and $0<f\in{\mathcal{C}}^{\infty}(\overline{\Omega}\setminus\{p\})$
with $f\in L^{p}(\Omega,dV)$ for some $p>1$. Fix $\lambda\in{\mathbb{R}}^{+}$.
Then there exists a unique plurisubharmonic function $u$ in $\Omega$
wich satisfies the following:


$\bullet$

$u$ is continuous on $\overline{\Omega}$ with u|∂Ω=ϕu_{|\partial\Omega}=\phi;



$\bullet$

$u$ is smooth in ${\Omega}\setminus\{p\}$



$\bullet$

$u$ satisfies $(dd^{c}u)^{n}=e^{\lambda u}fdV$.

results.title: Kähler-Einstein metrics with cone singularities on klt pairs
results.theorem: Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, $\alpha\in H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{R})$ a big class, and $\mu=fdV$ a volume form with density $f\geqslant 0$ belonging to $L^{1+\varepsilon}(dV)$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. Then there exists a unique $\theta$-psh function $\varphi$ with full Monge-Ampère mass such that $\langle(\theta+dd^{c}\varphi)^{n}\rangle=e^{\varphi}\mu$. Furthermore, $\varphi$ has minimal singularities.

results.title: Lelong numbers of currents of full mass intersection
results.theorem:
Let $\theta$ be a smooth closed $(1,1)$-form in a big cohomology class $\alpha$. Let $\varphi$ be a $\theta$-psh function of full Monge-Ampère mass, i.e,



$\{\langle(dd^{c}\varphi+\theta)^{n}\rangle\}=\langle\alpha^{n}\rangle.$



Let $\varphi_{\alpha,\min}$ be a $\theta$-psh function with minimal singularities. Then, we have



$\displaystyle\mathcal{I}(t\varphi)=\mathcal{I}(t\varphi_{\alpha,\min})$

(1.4)


for every $t>0$, where for every quasi-psh function $\psi$ on $X$, we denote by $\mathcal{I}(\psi)$ the multiplier ideal sheaf associated to $\psi$.

results.title: Degenerate complex Monge-Amp\` ere type equations on compact Hermitian manifolds and applications
results.theorem:
Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold of complex dimension $n$. Let $\beta$ be a smooth real $(1,1)$-form on $X$ such that there exists $\rho\in\mbox{PSH}(X,\beta)\cap L^{\infty}(X)$. Let $0\leq f\in L^{p}(X,\omega^{n})$, $p>1$, be such that $\int_{X}f\omega^{n}>0$. Let $\lambda>0$ be a positive number. Then there is a unique real-valued function $\varphi\in\mbox{PSH}(X,\beta)\cap L^{\infty}(X)$, satisfying



$(\beta+dd^{c}\varphi)^{n}=e^{\varphi}f\omega^{n}$



in the weak sense of currents, and $\|\varphi\|_{L^{\infty}(X)}\leq C(X,\omega,\beta,M,\|f\|_{p})$.

results.title: Géométrie d'Arakelov des variétés toriques et fibrés en droites intégrables
results.theorem:
Soient $\mathbb{P}(\Delta)$ une variété torique projective et lisse, et
$D$ un diviseur de Cartier horizontal $T$-invariant sur $\mathbb{P}(\Delta)$
tel que $\mathcal{O}(D)$ soit engendré par ses sections globales.
Pour tout ouvert $\Omega\subset\mathbb{P}(\Delta)(\mathbb{C})$ et pour toute
section holomorphe $s$ de $\mathcal{O}(D)(\mathbb{C})$ sur $\Omega$ ne s’annulant pas,
la fonction
$x\mapsto-\log\|s(x)\|_{D,\infty}^{2}$ est continue et plurisousharmonique sur $\Omega$.

results.title: Plurisupported Currents on Compact Kähler Manifolds
results.theorem:
Suppose that $\varphi\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta)$ and that $\varphi\leq 0$. Define the singularity type envelope:



$P_{\theta}[\varphi]:=\sup\{v\in\mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta)\ |\ v\leq 0,v\leq\varphi+\mathcal{O}(1)\}^{*},$

61:   In the present paper we ﬁrst give a more systematic treatment of these issues.
62: We explain how to deﬁne in a simple and canonical way the non-pluripolar product
63:                                      hT1 ∧ ... ∧ Tp i
64: of arbitrary closed positive (1, 1)-currents T1 , ..., Tp with 1 ≤ p ≤ n. The resulting
65: positive (p, p)-current hT1 ∧ ... ∧ Tp i puts no mass on pluripolar subsets. It is also
66: shown to be closed (Theorem 1.8), generalizing a classical result of Skoda-El Mir.

17: The chapter has a second, less obvious purpose.  Almost every theorem in
18: \cref{part:complex,part:comparisons} is a statement about a
19: \emph{singularity type}, and there are three inequivalent notions of
20: singularity type in circulation.  Two potentials may differ by a bounded

22: multiplier ideals.  The first relation is the finest, the third the

100: \subsection{Four comparisons, and why there are four}
101: \label{sec:ch51-four}
102: 
103: Let \(\varphi\) and \(\psi\) be quasi-psh functions on \(X\).  Four
104: relations between them occur in this book, and each is used somewhere in
105: \cref{part:complex,part:comparisons}:
106: \begin{enumerate}
107: \item pointwise order, \(\varphi\leq\psi\);
108: \item ordinary singularity type, \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), meaning
109:       \(\varphi\leq\psi+O(1)\);
110: \item \(P\)-comparison, \(\varphi\preceq_P\psi\), meaning
111:       \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\psi]\);
112: \item \(\mathcal I\)-comparison, \(\varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi\),
113:       meaning \(\mathcal I(m\varphi)\subseteq\mathcal I(m\psi)\) for every
114:       \(m\geq1\).
115: \end{enumerate}
116: Each is coarser than the one before it, and the induced equivalence
117: relations \(=\), \(\sim\), \(\sim_P\), \(\sim_{\mathcal I}\) are
118: correspondingly coarser.  The four are genuinely distinct.  Bounded
119: perturbations separate the first from the second.  The function
120: \(-\log(-\log|z|^2)\) of \Cref{ex:appH-loglog} separates the second from
121: the third: it is unbounded, hence not ordinarily equivalent to \(0\), but
122: its \(P\)-envelope is \(0\).  \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} separates the third
123: from the fourth, by exhibiting a potential all of whose Lelong numbers
124: vanish --- so that it is \(\mathcal I\)-equivalent to \(0\) --- but whose
125: nonpluripolar mass is \(1/2\) while the mass of \(0\) is \(1\).  The
126: \(P\)-projection theorem then forbids \(P\)-equivalence.
127: 
128: There is a useful mnemonic.  The relation \(\sim\) remembers the
129: potential up to a bounded error; \(\sim_P\) remembers exactly the
130: data that nonpluripolar masses and relative energies can see; and
131: \(\sim_{\mathcal I}\) remembers exactly the data that divisorial
132: valuations can see.  The last of these is what analytification produces
133: (\Cref{chap:valuative-analytification}), and it is also the datum on which
134: the analytic trace of \Cref{chap:operations-trace} depends.  The target of
135: that operator is nevertheless a \(P\)-class: every trace is
136: \(\mathcal I\)-good, and two choices are \(P\)-equivalent.  This upgrade
137: from \(\mathcal I\)-data at the source to \(P\)-uniqueness at the target is
138: a theorem about restricted quasi-equisingular approximants, not a formal
139: property of the three quotients.
140: 
141: \subsection{Standing hypotheses}

100: \subsection{Four comparisons, and why there are four}
101: \label{sec:ch51-four}
102: 
103: Let \(\varphi\) and \(\psi\) be quasi-psh functions on \(X\).  Four
104: relations between them occur in this book, and each is used somewhere in
105: \cref{part:complex,part:comparisons}:
106: \begin{enumerate}
107: \item pointwise order, \(\varphi\leq\psi\);
108: \item ordinary singularity type, \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), meaning
109:       \(\varphi\leq\psi+O(1)\);
110: \item \(P\)-comparison, \(\varphi\preceq_P\psi\), meaning
111:       \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\psi]\);
112: \item \(\mathcal I\)-comparison, \(\varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi\),
113:       meaning \(\mathcal I(m\varphi)\subseteq\mathcal I(m\psi)\) for every
114:       \(m\geq1\).
115: \end{enumerate}
116: Each is coarser than the one before it, and the induced equivalence
117: relations \(=\), \(\sim\), \(\sim_P\), \(\sim_{\mathcal I}\) are
118: correspondingly coarser.  The four are genuinely distinct.  Bounded
119: perturbations separate the first from the second.  The function
120: \(-\log(-\log|z|^2)\) of \Cref{ex:appH-loglog} separates the second from
121: the third: it is unbounded, hence not ordinarily equivalent to \(0\), but
122: its \(P\)-envelope is \(0\).  \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} separates the third
123: from the fourth, by exhibiting a potential all of whose Lelong numbers
124: vanish --- so that it is \(\mathcal I\)-equivalent to \(0\) --- but whose
125: nonpluripolar mass is \(1/2\) while the mass of \(0\) is \(1\).  The
126: \(P\)-projection theorem then forbids \(P\)-equivalence.
127: 
128: There is a useful mnemonic.  The relation \(\sim\) remembers the
129: potential up to a bounded error; \(\sim_P\) remembers exactly the
130: data that nonpluripolar masses and relative energies can see; and
131: \(\sim_{\mathcal I}\) remembers exactly the data that divisorial
132: valuations can see.  The last of these is what analytification produces
133: (\Cref{chap:valuative-analytification}), and it is also the datum on which
134: the analytic trace of \Cref{chap:operations-trace} depends.  The target of
135: that operator is nevertheless a \(P\)-class: every trace is
136: \(\mathcal I\)-good, and two choices are \(P\)-equivalent.  This upgrade
137: from \(\mathcal I\)-data at the source to \(P\)-uniqueness at the target is
138: a theorem about restricted quasi-equisingular approximants, not a formal
139: property of the three quotients.

2117: \label{sec:ch51-npp-bidegree-one}
2118: 
2119: In bidegree \((1,1)\) the nonpluripolar product has a completely explicit
2120: description, and every mass computation in this chapter uses it.
2121: 
2122: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:ch51-npp-bidegree-one}
2123: Let \(\varphi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\).  Then
2124: \[
2125:  \langle\theta_\varphi\rangle
2126:  =\one_{\{\varphi>-\infty\}}\,\theta_\varphi
2127: \]
2128: as measures on \(X\) when \(n=1\), and as currents in general.  In
2129: particular \(\langle\theta_\varphi\rangle\leq\theta_\varphi\), the two
2130: agree if and only if \(\theta_\varphi\) puts no mass on the pluripolar
2131: set \(\{\varphi=-\infty\}\), and, for \(n=1\),
2132: \[
2133:  M_\theta(\varphi)
2134:  =\int_X\theta_\varphi-\theta_\varphi(\{\varphi=-\infty\})
2135:  =\int_X\{\theta\}-\theta_\varphi(\{\varphi=-\infty\}).
2136: \]
2137: \end{lemma}
2138: 
2139: \begin{proof}
2140: Take \(p=1\) in \eqref{eq:complex-npp-truncation}.  With
2141: \(O_k=\{\varphi>-k\}\) and \(\varphi_k:=\max\{\varphi,-k\}\), plurifine
2142: locality gives
2143: \[
2144:  \one_{O_k}\theta_\varphi=\one_{O_k}\theta_{\varphi_k}
2145: \]
2146: for every \(k\), since \(\varphi=\varphi_k\) on \(O_k\).  The sets
2147: \(O_k\) increase to \(\{\varphi>-\infty\}\), so the increasing limit of
2148: the left-hand sides is \(\one_{\{\varphi>-\infty\}}\theta_\varphi\), while
2149: the increasing limit of the right-hand sides is by definition
2150: \(\langle\theta_\varphi\rangle\).  The inequality
2151: \(\langle\theta_\varphi\rangle\leq\theta_\varphi\) and the criterion for
2152: equality are immediate, and the mass formula for \(n=1\) follows because
2153: then \(\theta_\varphi\) is a positive measure of total mass
2154: \(\int_X\{\theta\}\), by Stokes.
2155: \end{proof}
2156: 
2157: \begin{remark}[The higher-degree analogue fails]
2158: \label{rem:ch51-npp-no-restriction}
2159: For \(p\geq2\) there is no formula
2160: \(\langle\theta_{\varphi_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_p}\rangle
2161: =\one_{\{\text{all }\varphi_j>-\infty\}}
2162: \theta_{\varphi_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_p}\), because the
2163: right-hand side has no meaning: the unrestricted product of unbounded
2164: potentials is not defined.  The nonpluripolar product is precisely the
2165: substitute, and \Cref{lem:ch51-npp-bidegree-one} is the one degree in
2166: which the substitute can be described by a restriction.  This is why the
2167: computations in \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} take place on a curve and the
2168: computations in \Cref{ex:ch51-blowup-mass} on a surface use a Siu
2169: decomposition instead.
2170: \end{remark}
2171: 
2172: \subsection{The ledger}
2173: \label{sec:ch51-npp-ledger}
2174: 
2175: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:complex-npp-ledger}
2176: The product \eqref{eq:complex-global-npp} is a closed positive
2177: \((p,p)\)-current.  It is symmetric and multilinear in the currents,
2178: local for the plurifine topology, agrees with the Bedford--Taylor
2179: product for locally bounded potentials, and charges no pluripolar set.
2180: If \(\varphi_j\) is replaced by a less singular potential in the same
2181: class, every mixed total mass can only increase.  Proper bimeromorphic
2182: pullback preserves total masses.
2183: \end{theorem}
2184: 
2185: \begin{proof}[Why truncation is sufficient]
2186: Plurifine locality makes the truncations in
2187: \eqref{eq:complex-npp-truncation} compatible.  Their masses on relatively
2188: compact sets are uniformly controlled after wedging with a K\"ahler
2189: form, so the increasing limit is locally finite.  Bedford--Taylor
2190: integration by parts yields closedness and symmetry before passage to
2191: the limit.  Monotonicity is the global theorem of
2192: \cite{BEGZ10}; bimeromorphic invariance follows by pulling the
2193: truncations to the common isomorphism locus, since the omitted sets are
2194: pluripolar.
2195: \end{proof}
2196: 
2197: The argument deserves to be run through once more, slowly, because five
2198: distinct assertions are packed into the statement and they have five
2199: different proofs.
2200: 
2201: \emph{Closedness, symmetry, multilinearity.}  Each truncated product
2202: \(\bigwedge_j\ddc\max\{u_j,-k\}\) is a closed positive current, symmetric
2203: and multilinear in its arguments, by Bedford--Taylor theory
2204: \cite{BT76,BT82}.  These properties are stable under the increasing limit
2205: of the restrictions \(\one_{O_k}(\cdot)\): positivity and symmetry are
2206: pointwise, multilinearity holds at each level \(k\), and closedness
2207: passes to the limit because a limit of closed currents in the weak
2208: topology is closed.
2209: 
2210: \emph{Plurifine locality.}  If \(u_j=v_j\) on a plurifine open set \(O\)
2211: for every \(j\), then the truncations coincide on
2212: \(O\cap O_k\), hence so do the limits on \(O\).  This is the property that
2213: makes the whole construction work, and it is
2214: \cite{BT87}.
2215: 
2216: \emph{Agreement with Bedford--Taylor.}  If every \(u_j\) is locally
2217: bounded, then \(O_k\) is the whole set for \(k\) large, and the
2218: truncations stabilize.
2219: 
2220: \emph{No mass on pluripolar sets.}  Assume that the increasing limit in
2221: \eqref{eq:complex-npp-truncation} is locally finite.  In the compact K\"ahler
2222: situation of \eqref{eq:complex-global-npp}, this local finiteness follows from
2223: \cite[Proposition~1.6]{BEGZ10}.  Let \(A\) be a Borel pluripolar set.  Work
2224: on coordinate balls \(V\Subset V'\Subset U\), with \(V'\) strongly
2225: pseudoconvex.  Choose a smooth strictly psh function \(\rho\) on a
2226: neighbourhood of \(\overline{V'}\), and set \(\beta:=\ddc\rho\).  Recall
2227: that the Bedford--Taylor capacity and its outer capacity are
2228: \[
2229:  \Capa_{\mathrm{BT}}(E,V')
2230:  :=\sup_{\substack{q\in\PSH(V')\\0<q<1}}
2231:        \int_E(\ddc q)^n,
2232:  \qquad
2233:  \Capa_{\mathrm{BT}}^*(E,V')
2234:  :=\inf_{\substack{G\supset E\\G\ \mathrm{open}}}
2235:        \Capa_{\mathrm{BT}}(G,V').
2236: \]
2237: For fixed \(k\), every
2238: \(w_{j,k}:=\max\{u_j,-k\}\) is locally bounded and psh.  The mixed
2239: Bedford--Taylor measure
2240: \[
2241:  \nu_k:=\one_{O_k}\bigwedge_{j=1}^p\ddc w_{j,k}
2242:                    \wedge\beta^{n-p}
2243: \]
2244: vanishes on \(A\cap V\).  Indeed, each \(w_{j,k}\) is bounded on \(V'\)
2245: because \(\overline{V'}\Subset U\), and \(\rho\) is bounded there because
2246: it is smooth on a neighbourhood of \(\overline{V'}\).  After adding
2247: constants and multiplying by positive scalars, normalize the \(p\) functions
2248: \(w_{j,k}\) and the \(n-p\) copies of \(\rho\) to functions with values in
2249: \((0,1)\) on \(V'\).  Denote the normalized functions by
2250: \(f_i=a_i h_i+b_i\), where
2251: \((h_1,\ldots,h_n)=(w_{1,k},\ldots,w_{p,k},\rho,\ldots,\rho)\) and
2252: \(a_i>0\), and put \(W=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i\).  Positivity and
2253: multilinearity give
2254: \[
2255:  (\ddc W)^n\geq\frac{n!}{n^n}\bigwedge_{i=1}^n\ddc f_i
2256:  =\frac{n!}{n^n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^na_i\right)
2257:    \bigwedge_{j=1}^p\ddc w_{j,k}\wedge\beta^{n-p}.
2258: \]
2259: Consequently, for Borel \(E\subset V\),
2260: \[
2261:  \nu_k(E)\leq C_k\int_E(\ddc W)^n
2262:              \leq C_k\Capa_{\mathrm{BT}}^*(E,V').
2263: \]
2264: Here the first inequality also uses the fact that restriction by
2265: \(\one_{O_k}\) can only decrease a positive measure.  A pluripolar set has
2266: zero Bedford--Taylor outer capacity
2267: \cite[Theorem~6.9]{BT82}.  Finally, the currents in
2268: \eqref{eq:complex-npp-truncation} increase to the nonpluripolar product, so
2269: their trace measures \(\nu_k\) increase to its trace measure on \(V\).
2270: Continuity from below therefore gives
2271: \[
2272:  \left(\left\langle\bigwedge_{j=1}^p\ddc u_j\right\rangle
2273:        \wedge\beta^{n-p}\right)(A\cap V)
2274:  =\lim_k\nu_k(A\cap V)=0.
2275: \]
2276: Since \(V\) is arbitrary, the product charges no pluripolar set.
2277: 
2278: \emph{Monotonicity of total masses.}  If
2279: \(\varphi_j\preceq\psi_j\) for every \(j\), with \(\psi_j\) in the same
2280: class, then
2281: \[
2282:  \int_X\langle\theta_{\varphi_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\varphi_p}
2283:  \wedge\omega^{n-p}\rangle
2284:  \leq
2285:  \int_X\langle\theta_{\psi_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\theta_{\psi_p}
2286:  \wedge\omega^{n-p}\rangle .
2287: \]
2288: This is \emph{not} a pointwise inequality between the two currents, and it
2289: is not proved by integration by parts on the truncations, because the
2290: error terms supported on the truncation boundaries do not obviously
2291: vanish.  The unrestricted statement is
2292: \cite[Theorem~1.1]{DDNL18mono}; its predecessor, under the hypothesis that
2293: the potentials have small unbounded locus, is
2294: \cite[Theorem~1.16]{BEGZ10}.  We import the former.
2295: 
2296: \emph{Bimeromorphic invariance.}  Let \(\pi:Y\to X\) be a modification
2297: with exceptional locus \(F\) and indeterminacy locus of \(\pi^{-1}\)
2298: equal to \(Z=\pi(F)\).  Both \(F\) and \(Z\) are pluripolar --- they are
2299: proper analytic subsets --- so no mass sits on them.  On the complement,
2300: \(\pi\) is a biholomorphism and the change-of-variables formula applies
2301: term by term to the truncations.  Hence each mixed total mass is
2302: preserved.  This is the statement used in
2303: \Cref{thm:tna-bimeromorphic}.
2304: 
2305: \begin{warning}{Monotonicity is about masses, not measures}
2306: \label{warn:ch51-monotonicity}
2307: \Cref{thm:complex-npp-ledger} asserts that replacing a potential by a
2308: less singular one in the same class can only increase the \emph{total}
2309: mixed masses.  It does not assert any inequality between the two
2310: Monge--Amp\`ere measures.  On \(\mathbf P^1\), take \(\varphi=\max\{G_0,
2311: -1\}\) and \(\psi=0\): both have mass \(1\), yet
2312: \(\MA_\omega(\varphi)\) charges a circle and \(\MA_\omega(\psi)=\omega\)
2313: does not.  This is computed in \Cref{ex:ch51-p1-envelope}.
2314: \end{warning}

{"source_id":"p148_ch51_dependency_v4","source_sha256":"7f2b4890d6332d042113d89bfa921f0f58bbfcbd63c5a18a9eff21469a0fc40b","start_line":3223,"end_line":3299,"text":"3223: \subsection{The \texorpdfstring{\(\mathcal I\)}{I}-preorder}
3224: \label{sec:ch51-i-preorder}
3225: 
3226: \begin{definition}[\(\mathcal I\)-preorder]
3227: \label{def:complex-i-preorder}
3228: For quasi-psh \(\varphi,\psi\), write
3229: \[
3230:  \varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi
3231:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
3232:  \mathcal I(m\varphi)\subseteq\mathcal I(m\psi)
3233:  \quad\text{for every }m\geq1.
3234: \tag{51.26}\label{eq:complex-i-preorder}
3235: \]
3236: Equivalently, \(\nu(\varphi,E)\geq\nu(\psi,E)\) for every prime divisor
3237: over \(X\).  Write \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}\psi\) for equality in both
3238: directions.
3239: \end{definition}
3240: 
3241: The asserted equivalence of the two descriptions is
3242: \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3243: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, applied to the pair of one-sided
3244: statements; note that the ideal inclusion and the Lelong inequality point
3245: in opposite directions, because a more singular potential has larger
3246: Lelong numbers and smaller multiplier ideals.  Reading the direction
3247: backwards is the commonest error in this circle of ideas, and it is
3248: detected by the one-pole test of \Cref{sec:ch51-unit-tests}: with
3249: \(\varphi=\log|z|^2\) and \(\psi=0\) one has
3250: \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), \(\nu(\varphi,0)=1>0=\nu(\psi,0)\), and
3251: \(\mathcal I(\varphi)=(z)\subsetneq\cO=\mathcal I(\psi)\).
3252: 
3253: \begin{proposition}
3254: \label{prop:ch51-i-calculus}
3255: Let \(\varphi,\psi,\varphi',\psi'\) be quasi-psh on \(X\) and

3227: \label{def:complex-i-preorder}
3228: For quasi-psh \(\varphi,\psi\), write
3229: \[
3230:  \varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi
3231:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
3232:  \mathcal I(m\varphi)\subseteq\mathcal I(m\psi)
3233:  \quad\text{for every }m\geq1.
3234: \tag{51.26}\label{eq:complex-i-preorder}
3235: \]
3236: Equivalently, \(\nu(\varphi,E)\geq\nu(\psi,E)\) for every prime divisor
3237: over \(X\).  Write \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}\psi\) for equality in both
3238: directions.
3239: \end{definition}
3240: 
3241: The asserted equivalence of the two descriptions is
3242: \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3243: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, applied to the pair of one-sided
3244: statements; note that the ideal inclusion and the Lelong inequality point
3245: in opposite directions, because a more singular potential has larger
3246: Lelong numbers and smaller multiplier ideals.  Reading the direction
3247: backwards is the commonest error in this circle of ideas, and it is
3248: detected by the one-pole test of \Cref{sec:ch51-unit-tests}: with
3249: \(\varphi=\log|z|^2\) and \(\psi=0\) one has
3250: \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), \(\nu(\varphi,0)=1>0=\nu(\psi,0)\), and
3251: \(\mathcal I(\varphi)=(z)\subsetneq\cO=\mathcal I(\psi)\).

3301: \label{sec:ch51-i-envelope-def}
3302: 
3303: \begin{definition}[\(\mathcal I\)-envelope]
3304: \label{def:complex-i-envelope}
3305: For \(\varphi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\), set
3306: \[
3307:  P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}
3308:  :=\uscsup\{\psi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\mid
3309:           \psi\leq0,\ \psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\}.
3310: \tag{51.27}\label{eq:complex-i-envelope}
3311: \]
3312: It is \(\mathcal I\)-model if it is fixed by this operator.
3313: \end{definition}
3314: 
3315: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:complex-i-projection}
3316: For every \(\varphi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\),
3317: \[
3318:  \varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},
3319: \qquad
3320:  P_\theta[P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}]_{\mathcal I}
3321:       =P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}.
3322: \tag{51.28}\label{eq:complex-i-projection}
3323: \]
3324: Furthermore,
3325: \[
3326:  P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},
3327: \qquad
3328:  \varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi].
3329: \tag{51.29}\label{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}
3330: \]
3331: If \(\varphi\) has analytic singularities, then
3332: \[
3333:  \varphi\sim P_\theta[\varphi]
3334:         \sim P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}.
3335: \tag{51.30}\label{eq:complex-analytic-envelope-agreement}
3336: \]
3337: \end{theorem}
3338: 
3339: \begin{proof}
3340: Choquet reduction replaces the family in
3341: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope} by an increasing sequence.  Finite maxima
3342: preserve divisorial Lelong numbers, and strong openness shows that its
3343: usc supremum has the same multiplier ideals as \(\varphi\).  This proves
3344: \eqref{eq:complex-i-projection}.  Formula
3345: \eqref{eq:complex-p-envelope-rooftop}, again with strong openness, gives
3346: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]\), hence
3347: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}.  For analytic singularities, pass to
3348: a log resolution.  Divisorial orders then control the whole singularity
3349: up to \(O(1)\), so the two envelopes cannot be strictly less singular
3350: than \(\varphi\).
3351: \end{proof}
3352: 
3353: \begin{proof}[The steps in full]
3354: Write \(F:=\{\psi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\mid\psi\leq0,\
3355: \psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\}\) for the competitor family in
3356: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope}.
3357: 
3358: \emph{Step 1: \(F\) is nonempty and directed.}  It contains
3359: \(\varphi-\sup_X\varphi\).  If \(\psi_1,\psi_2\in F\), then
3360: \(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\}\in\PSH(X,\theta)\) by
3361: \Cref{prop:ch51-psh-operations}, item \cref{itm:ch51-op:max}, it is
3362: \(\leq0\), and by \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item
3363: \cref{itm:ch51-lc:max}, applied at a generic point of each prime divisor
3364: \(E\) over \(X\),
3365: \[
3366:  \nu(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\},E)
3367:  =\min\{\nu(\psi_1,E),\nu(\psi_2,E)\}
3368:  =\nu(\varphi,E).
3369: \]
3370: Hence \(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\}\in F\), and \(F\) is directed.
3371: 
3372: \emph{Step 2: the envelope lies in \(F\), which gives
3373: \eqref{eq:complex-i-projection}.}  By Step 1 and
3374: \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing},
3375: \[
3376:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},E\bigr)
3377:  =\inf_{\psi\in F}\nu(\psi,E)
3378:  =\nu(\varphi,E)
3379: \]
3380: for every prime divisor \(E\) over \(X\).  Since
3381: \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\leq0\), this says
3382: \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\in F\); it is therefore the largest
3383: element of \(F\), and in particular
3384: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\).  As \(F\)
3385: depends only on the \(\mathcal I\)-class of \(\varphi\), the family
3386: attached to \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\) is the same \(F\), and
3387: idempotence follows.
3388: 
3389: \emph{Step 3: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]\).}  By Step 1
3390: of the proof of \Cref{thm:complex-p-projection}, the rooftops
3391: \(u_C=(\varphi+C)\wedge_\theta V_\theta\) satisfy \(u_C\sim\varphi\) for
3392: \(C\) large, hence \(\nu(u_C,E)=\nu(\varphi,E)\) for every \(E\) by
3393: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lc:bounded}.  The
3394: family \((u_C)\) is increasing, and
3395: \(P_\theta[\varphi]=\uscsup_Cu_C\); so
3396: \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing} gives
3397: \(\nu(P_\theta[\varphi],E)=\nu(\varphi,E)\), which is the second half of
3398: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}.  This step uses no positivity of
3399: mass.
3400: 
3401: \emph{Step 4: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\).}
3402: By Step 3 and \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq V_\theta\leq0\), the potential
3403: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\) belongs to \(F\); by Step 2 it is therefore at most
3404: the largest element of \(F\).
3405: 
3406: \emph{Step 5: analytic singularities.}  Assume \(\varphi\) has analytic
3407: singularities, and let \(\rho:Z\to X\) be a log resolution with
3408: \[
3409:  \rho^*\varphi=c\log|s_D|_h^2+O(1),
3410: \]
3411: \(D\) an effective divisor with simple normal crossing support, \(h\) a
3412: smooth metric on \(\cO_Z(D)\), and \(c>0\).  Put
3413: \(\Psi:=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\), which by Step 2 satisfies
3414: \(\Psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\).  By
3415: \Cref{prop:ch51-divisorial-calculus}, items
3416: \cref{itm:ch51-dc:pullback} and \cref{itm:ch51-dc:analytic}, for every
3417: prime divisor \(E\subset Z\),
3418: \[
3419:  \nu(\rho^*\Psi,E)=\nu(\Psi,E)=\nu(\varphi,E)=c\,\ord_E(D).
3420: \]
3421: The Siu decomposition of \Cref{sec:ch51-divisorial}, applied to the
3422: closed positive current \(\rho^*\theta+\ddc\rho^*\Psi\), therefore gives
3423: \[
3424:  \rho^*\theta+\ddc\rho^*\Psi\ \geq\ c\,[D].
3425: \]
3426: Writing \(\Theta_D=c_1(\cO_Z(D),h)\) and using Poincar\'e--Lelong
3427: \eqref{eq:appJ-complex-section-pl} in the form
3428: \(\ddc\log|s_D|_h^2=[D]-\Theta_D\), we obtain
3429: \[
3430:  \bigl(\rho^*\theta-c\,\Theta_D\bigr)
3431:  +\ddc\bigl(\rho^*\Psi-c\log|s_D|_h^2\bigr)\ \geq\ 0 ,
3432: \]
3433: so \(\rho^*\Psi-c\log|s_D|_h^2\) is quasi-psh on the compact manifold
3434: \(Z\), hence bounded above.  Thus
3435: \(\rho^*\Psi\leq c\log|s_D|_h^2+C=\rho^*\varphi+C'\), and since \(\rho\)
3436: is an isomorphism over a dense open subset of \(X\) and both sides are
3437: upper semicontinuous, \(\Psi\preceq\varphi\).  Combining with
3438: \(\varphi\preceq P_\theta[\varphi]\leq\Psi\) from
3439: \Cref{prop:ch51-p-elementary}, item \cref{itm:ch51-pe:above}, and Step 4,
3440: \[
3441:  \varphi\ \sim\ P_\theta[\varphi]\ \sim\ P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},
3442: \]
3443: which is \eqref{eq:complex-analytic-envelope-agreement}.
3444: \end{proof}
3445: 
3446: \begin{corollary}[Canonical reconstruction from realizable
3447: \texorpdfstring{\(\mathcal I\)}{I}-data]
3448: \label{cor:ch51-i-canonical-reconstruction}
3449: For a realizable \(\mathcal I\)-class
3450: \(d=[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\) in \(\PSH(X,\theta)\), the formula
3451: \[
3452:  \mathcal R_\theta(d):=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}
3453: \]
3454: is well defined.  It is the unique \(\mathcal I\)-model potential in the
3455: class \(d\) with \(\sup_X\mathcal R_\theta(d)=0\).  Thus realizable
3456: \(\mathcal I\)-data determines its canonical normalized
3457: \(\mathcal I\)-model representative, without a positive-mass hypothesis.
3458: \end{corollary}
3459: 
3460: \begin{proof}
3461: The competitor family in \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope} depends only on
3462: \(d\).  The proof of \Cref{thm:complex-i-projection} shows that its
3463: envelope lies in that family and is its largest element; the formula is
3464: therefore well defined.  The second identity in that theorem says that the
3465: output is \(\mathcal I\)-model.  It is at most zero by
3466: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope}.  If its supremum were strictly negative,
3467: adding a sufficiently small positive constant would give another competitor
3468: in the same defining family, contradicting maximality.  Finally, a
3469: normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model potential in the class \(d\) is the fixed
3470: point of the envelope attached to that same competitor family, and hence is
3471: \(\mathcal R_\theta(d)\).
3472: \end{proof}
3473: 
3474: \begin{remark}[Where each hypothesis is used]
3475: \label{rem:ch51-i-projection-hypotheses}
3476: Steps 1--4 use no positivity of mass and no regularity of \(\varphi\);
3477: they are consequences of \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing} and the
3478: minimum rule for maxima.  Step 5 uses resolution of singularities and
3479: Siu's decomposition, and it is the only step that upgrades an
3480: \(\mathcal I\)-statement to an ordinary-type statement.  It is essential
3481: that the upgrade is applied to the \emph{envelope} \(\Psi\) and not to an
3482: arbitrary competitor: the argument produces a constant \(C'\) depending
3483: on \(\Psi\), and no uniform constant over the whole family \(F\) is
3484: claimed or needed.
3485: \end{remark}
3486: 
3487: \begin{warning}{Do not read Step 5 as a general rigidity statement}
3488: \label{warn:ch51-step5}
3489: Step 5 does \emph{not} say that two potentials with the same divisorial
3490: Lelong numbers have bounded difference.  It says that the
3491: \(\mathcal I\)-envelope of a potential with analytic singularities has
3492: bounded difference from it.  The general statement is false, by
3493: \Cref{ex:ch51-disk-three-types}; and the difference is not merely
3494: cosmetic, since \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} produces an
3495: \(\mathcal I\)-equivalent pair with different nonpluripolar masses.
3496: \end{warning}
3497: 
3498: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:complex-comparison-hierarchy}
3499: For quasi-psh functions,
3500: \[
3501:  \varphi\preceq\psi
3502:  \Longrightarrow
3503:  \varphi\preceq_P\psi
3504:  \Longrightarrow
3505:  \varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi.
3506: \tag{51.31}\label{eq:complex-comparison-hierarchy}
3507: \]
3508: Neither reverse implication is asserted.  In particular,
3509: \(\mathcal I\)-equivalence is coarser than \(P\)-equivalence.
3510: \end{corollary}
3511: 
3512: \begin{proof}
3513: If \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), then every normalized competitor defining
3514: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\) is also a competitor for \(P_\theta[\psi]\), which
3515: gives the first implication.  The second follows from
3516: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}: applying the \(\mathcal I\)-envelope
3517: to the ordered \(P\)-envelopes gives the corresponding
3518: \(\mathcal I\)-order.  Applying both implications in both directions
3519: gives the assertion about equivalence relations.
3520: \end{proof}
3521: 
3522: \begin{proof}[The second implication, in detail]
3523: Assume \(\varphi\preceq_P\psi\), that is
3524: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\psi]\) for a common background in which
3525: both have positive mass.  Monotonicity of Lelong numbers under the
3526: pointwise order, which is \eqref{eq:complex-lelong-number}, gives
3527: \[
3528:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\varphi],E\bigr)
3529:  \ \geq\
3530:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\psi],E\bigr)
3531: \]
3532: for every prime divisor \(E\) over \(X\), the inequality reversing
3533: because a smaller potential is more singular.  By Step 3 of the proof of
3534: \Cref{thm:complex-i-projection}, the two sides equal
3535: \(\nu(\varphi,E)\) and \(\nu(\psi,E)\) respectively.  Hence
3536: \[
3537:  \nu(\varphi,E)\ \geq\ \nu(\psi,E)
3538:  \qquad\text{for every prime divisor }E\text{ over }X,
3539: \]
3540: which by \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3541: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, and
3542: \Cref{def:complex-i-preorder} is exactly
3543: \(\varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi\).  Note that the conclusion does not
3544: mention \(\theta\), consistently with
3545: \Cref{prop:ch51-i-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-ic:preorder}.
3546: \end{proof}
3547: 
3548: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:ch51-quotient-maps}
3549: There are canonical surjections of preordered sets
3550: \[
3551:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim}
3552:  \ \longrightarrow\
3553:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim_P}
3554:  \ \longrightarrow\
3555:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim_{\mathcal I}} ,
3556: \]
3557: where the middle quotient is taken on the locus of potentials of
3558: positive mass in a fixed sufficiently positive background.  Both maps are
3559: strictly non-injective:
3560: \Cref{ex:appH-loglog} separates the first two, and
3561: \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} separates the last two.
3562: \end{corollary}
3563: 
3564: \begin{proof}
3565: The maps exist and are order preserving by
3566: \Cref{cor:complex-comparison-hierarchy}, and they are surjective because
3567: each is induced by the identity on representatives.  The separations are
3568: the cited examples.
3569: \end{proof}
3570: 
3571: The chain of \Cref{cor:ch51-quotient-maps} is the source of the
3572: factorization \eqref{eq:verified-trace-factorization}: the trace of
3573: \Cref{chap:operations-trace} depends only on the input
3574: \(\mathcal I\)-class but lands in a well-defined output \(P\)-class.
3575: Hence the map obtained by starting with input \(P\)-classes factors through
3576: the second surjection above.  \Cref{thm:verified-trace-factorization}
3577: records this asymmetric, source-backed factorization.
3578: "}
