3339: \begin{proof}
3340: Choquet reduction replaces the family in
3341: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope} by an increasing sequence.  Finite maxima
3342: preserve divisorial Lelong numbers, and strong openness shows that its
3343: usc supremum has the same multiplier ideals as \(\varphi\).  This proves
3344: \eqref{eq:complex-i-projection}.  Formula
3345: \eqref{eq:complex-p-envelope-rooftop}, again with strong openness, gives
3346: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]\), hence
3347: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}.  For analytic singularities, pass to
3348: a log resolution.  Divisorial orders then control the whole singularity
3349: up to \(O(1)\), so the two envelopes cannot be strictly less singular
3350: than \(\varphi\).
3351: \end{proof}
3352: 
3353: \begin{proof}[The steps in full]
3354: Write \(F:=\{\psi\in\PSH(X,\theta)\mid\psi\leq0,\
3355: \psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\}\) for the competitor family in
3356: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope}.
3357: 
3358: \emph{Step 1: \(F\) is nonempty and directed.}  It contains
3359: \(\varphi-\sup_X\varphi\).  If \(\psi_1,\psi_2\in F\), then
3360: \(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\}\in\PSH(X,\theta)\) by
3361: \Cref{prop:ch51-psh-operations}, item \cref{itm:ch51-op:max}, it is
3362: \(\leq0\), and by \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item
3363: \cref{itm:ch51-lc:max}, applied at a generic point of each prime divisor
3364: \(E\) over \(X\),
3365: \[
3366:  \nu(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\},E)
3367:  =\min\{\nu(\psi_1,E),\nu(\psi_2,E)\}
3368:  =\nu(\varphi,E).
3369: \]
3370: Hence \(\max\{\psi_1,\psi_2\}\in F\), and \(F\) is directed.
3371: 
3372: \emph{Step 2: the envelope lies in \(F\), which gives
3373: \eqref{eq:complex-i-projection}.}  By Step 1 and
3374: \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing},
3375: \[
3376:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},E\bigr)
3377:  =\inf_{\psi\in F}\nu(\psi,E)
3378:  =\nu(\varphi,E)
3379: \]
3380: for every prime divisor \(E\) over \(X\).  Since
3381: \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\leq0\), this says
3382: \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\in F\); it is therefore the largest
3383: element of \(F\), and in particular
3384: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\).  As \(F\)
3385: depends only on the \(\mathcal I\)-class of \(\varphi\), the family
3386: attached to \(P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\) is the same \(F\), and
3387: idempotence follows.
3388: 
3389: \emph{Step 3: \(\varphi\sim_{\mathcal I}P_\theta[\varphi]\).}  By Step 1
3390: of the proof of \Cref{thm:complex-p-projection}, the rooftops
3391: \(u_C=(\varphi+C)\wedge_\theta V_\theta\) satisfy \(u_C\sim\varphi\) for
3392: \(C\) large, hence \(\nu(u_C,E)=\nu(\varphi,E)\) for every \(E\) by
3393: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lc:bounded}.  The
3394: family \((u_C)\) is increasing, and
3395: \(P_\theta[\varphi]=\uscsup_Cu_C\); so
3396: \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing} gives
3397: \(\nu(P_\theta[\varphi],E)=\nu(\varphi,E)\), which is the second half of
3398: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}.  This step uses no positivity of
3399: mass.
3400: 
3401: \emph{Step 4: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\).}
3402: By Step 3 and \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq V_\theta\leq0\), the potential
3403: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\) belongs to \(F\); by Step 2 it is therefore at most
3404: the largest element of \(F\).
3405: 
3406: \emph{Step 5: analytic singularities.}  Assume \(\varphi\) has analytic
3407: singularities, and let \(\rho:Z\to X\) be a log resolution with
3408: \[
3409:  \rho^*\varphi=c\log|s_D|_h^2+O(1),
3410: \]
3411: \(D\) an effective divisor with simple normal crossing support, \(h\) a
3412: smooth metric on \(\cO_Z(D)\), and \(c>0\).  Put
3413: \(\Psi:=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\), which by Step 2 satisfies
3414: \(\Psi\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi\).  By
3415: \Cref{prop:ch51-divisorial-calculus}, items
3416: \cref{itm:ch51-dc:pullback} and \cref{itm:ch51-dc:analytic}, for every
3417: prime divisor \(E\subset Z\),
3418: \[
3419:  \nu(\rho^*\Psi,E)=\nu(\Psi,E)=\nu(\varphi,E)=c\,\ord_E(D).
3420: \]
3421: The Siu decomposition of \Cref{sec:ch51-divisorial}, applied to the
3422: closed positive current \(\rho^*\theta+\ddc\rho^*\Psi\), therefore gives
3423: \[
3424:  \rho^*\theta+\ddc\rho^*\Psi\ \geq\ c\,[D].
3425: \]
3426: Writing \(\Theta_D=c_1(\cO_Z(D),h)\) and using Poincar\'e--Lelong
3427: \eqref{eq:appJ-complex-section-pl} in the form
3428: \(\ddc\log|s_D|_h^2=[D]-\Theta_D\), we obtain
3429: \[
3430:  \bigl(\rho^*\theta-c\,\Theta_D\bigr)
3431:  +\ddc\bigl(\rho^*\Psi-c\log|s_D|_h^2\bigr)\ \geq\ 0 ,
3432: \]
3433: so \(\rho^*\Psi-c\log|s_D|_h^2\) is quasi-psh on the compact manifold
3434: \(Z\), hence bounded above.  Thus
3435: \(\rho^*\Psi\leq c\log|s_D|_h^2+C=\rho^*\varphi+C'\), and since \(\rho\)
3436: is an isomorphism over a dense open subset of \(X\) and both sides are
3437: upper semicontinuous, \(\Psi\preceq\varphi\).  Combining with
3438: \(\varphi\preceq P_\theta[\varphi]\leq\Psi\) from
3439: \Cref{prop:ch51-p-elementary}, item \cref{itm:ch51-pe:above}, and Step 4,
3440: \[
3441:  \varphi\ \sim\ P_\theta[\varphi]\ \sim\ P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I},
3442: \]
3443: which is \eqref{eq:complex-analytic-envelope-agreement}.
3444: \end{proof}
3445: 
3446: \begin{corollary}[Canonical reconstruction from realizable
3447: \texorpdfstring{\(\mathcal I\)}{I}-data]
3448: \label{cor:ch51-i-canonical-reconstruction}
3449: For a realizable \(\mathcal I\)-class
3450: \(d=[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}\) in \(\PSH(X,\theta)\), the formula
3451: \[
3452:  \mathcal R_\theta(d):=P_\theta[\varphi]_{\mathcal I}
3453: \]
3454: is well defined.  It is the unique \(\mathcal I\)-model potential in the
3455: class \(d\) with \(\sup_X\mathcal R_\theta(d)=0\).  Thus realizable
3456: \(\mathcal I\)-data determines its canonical normalized
3457: \(\mathcal I\)-model representative, without a positive-mass hypothesis.
3458: \end{corollary}
3459: 
3460: \begin{proof}
3461: The competitor family in \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope} depends only on
3462: \(d\).  The proof of \Cref{thm:complex-i-projection} shows that its
3463: envelope lies in that family and is its largest element; the formula is
3464: therefore well defined.  The second identity in that theorem says that the
3465: output is \(\mathcal I\)-model.  It is at most zero by
3466: \eqref{eq:complex-i-envelope}.  If its supremum were strictly negative,
3467: adding a sufficiently small positive constant would give another competitor
3468: in the same defining family, contradicting maximality.  Finally, a
3469: normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model potential in the class \(d\) is the fixed
3470: point of the envelope attached to that same competitor family, and hence is
3471: \(\mathcal R_\theta(d)\).
3472: \end{proof}
3473: 
3474: \begin{remark}[Where each hypothesis is used]
3475: \label{rem:ch51-i-projection-hypotheses}
3476: Steps 1--4 use no positivity of mass and no regularity of \(\varphi\);
3477: they are consequences of \Cref{lem:ch51-lelong-increasing} and the
3478: minimum rule for maxima.  Step 5 uses resolution of singularities and
3479: Siu's decomposition, and it is the only step that upgrades an
3480: \(\mathcal I\)-statement to an ordinary-type statement.  It is essential
3481: that the upgrade is applied to the \emph{envelope} \(\Psi\) and not to an
3482: arbitrary competitor: the argument produces a constant \(C'\) depending
3483: on \(\Psi\), and no uniform constant over the whole family \(F\) is
3484: claimed or needed.
3485: \end{remark}
3486: 
3487: \begin{warning}{Do not read Step 5 as a general rigidity statement}
3488: \label{warn:ch51-step5}
3489: Step 5 does \emph{not} say that two potentials with the same divisorial
3490: Lelong numbers have bounded difference.  It says that the
3491: \(\mathcal I\)-envelope of a potential with analytic singularities has
3492: bounded difference from it.  The general statement is false, by
3493: \Cref{ex:ch51-disk-three-types}; and the difference is not merely
3494: cosmetic, since \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} produces an
3495: \(\mathcal I\)-equivalent pair with different nonpluripolar masses.
3496: \end{warning}
3497: 
3498: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:complex-comparison-hierarchy}
3499: For quasi-psh functions,
3500: \[
3501:  \varphi\preceq\psi
3502:  \Longrightarrow
3503:  \varphi\preceq_P\psi
3504:  \Longrightarrow
3505:  \varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi.
3506: \tag{51.31}\label{eq:complex-comparison-hierarchy}
3507: \]
3508: Neither reverse implication is asserted.  In particular,
3509: \(\mathcal I\)-equivalence is coarser than \(P\)-equivalence.
3510: \end{corollary}
3511: 
3512: \begin{proof}
3513: If \(\varphi\preceq\psi\), then every normalized competitor defining
3514: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\) is also a competitor for \(P_\theta[\psi]\), which
3515: gives the first implication.  The second follows from
3516: \eqref{eq:complex-p-i-comparison}: applying the \(\mathcal I\)-envelope
3517: to the ordered \(P\)-envelopes gives the corresponding
3518: \(\mathcal I\)-order.  Applying both implications in both directions
3519: gives the assertion about equivalence relations.
3520: \end{proof}
3521: 
3522: \begin{proof}[The second implication, in detail]
3523: Assume \(\varphi\preceq_P\psi\), that is
3524: \(P_\theta[\varphi]\leq P_\theta[\psi]\) for a common background in which
3525: both have positive mass.  Monotonicity of Lelong numbers under the
3526: pointwise order, which is \eqref{eq:complex-lelong-number}, gives
3527: \[
3528:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\varphi],E\bigr)
3529:  \ \geq\
3530:  \nu\bigl(P_\theta[\psi],E\bigr)
3531: \]
3532: for every prime divisor \(E\) over \(X\), the inequality reversing
3533: because a smaller potential is more singular.  By Step 3 of the proof of
3534: \Cref{thm:complex-i-projection}, the two sides equal
3535: \(\nu(\varphi,E)\) and \(\nu(\psi,E)\) respectively.  Hence
3536: \[
3537:  \nu(\varphi,E)\ \geq\ \nu(\psi,E)
3538:  \qquad\text{for every prime divisor }E\text{ over }X,
3539: \]
3540: which by \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3541: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, and
3542: \Cref{def:complex-i-preorder} is exactly
3543: \(\varphi\preceq_{\mathcal I}\psi\).  Note that the conclusion does not
3544: mention \(\theta\), consistently with
3545: \Cref{prop:ch51-i-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-ic:preorder}.
3546: \end{proof}
3547: 
3548: \begin{corollary}\label{cor:ch51-quotient-maps}
3549: There are canonical surjections of preordered sets
3550: \[
3551:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim}
3552:  \ \longrightarrow\
3553:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim_P}
3554:  \ \longrightarrow\
3555:  \QPSH(X)/{\sim_{\mathcal I}} ,
3556: \]
3557: where the middle quotient is taken on the locus of potentials of
3558: positive mass in a fixed sufficiently positive background.  Both maps are
3559: strictly non-injective:
3560: \Cref{ex:appH-loglog} separates the first two, and
3561: \Cref{ex:ch51-cantor} separates the last two.
3562: \end{corollary}
3563: 
3564: \begin{proof}
3565: The maps exist and are order preserving by
3566: \Cref{cor:complex-comparison-hierarchy}, and they are surjective because
3567: each is induced by the identity on representatives.  The separations are
3568: the cited examples.
3569: \end{proof}
3570: 
3571: The chain of \Cref{cor:ch51-quotient-maps} is the source of the
3572: factorization \eqref{eq:verified-trace-factorization}: the trace of
3573: \Cref{chap:operations-trace} depends only on the input
3574: \(\mathcal I\)-class but lands in a well-defined output \(P\)-class.
3575: Hence the map obtained by starting with input \(P\)-classes factors through
3576: the second surjection above.  \Cref{thm:verified-trace-factorization}
3577: records this asymmetric, source-backed factorization.

3798: The construction uses one classical input: a compact set of vanishing
3799: logarithmic capacity carrying a probability measure without atoms.  We
3800: recall it explicitly so that the numbers below can be checked.
3801: 
3802: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:ch51-polar-cantor}
3803: Let \((\ell_m)_{m\geq0}\) be lengths with \(\ell_0=1\) and
3804: \(\ell_{m+1}\leq\ell_m/2\), and let
3805: \(F=\bigcap_mF_m\subset[0,1]\subset\mathbf C\) be the generalized Cantor
3806: set in which \(F_m\) is a disjoint union of \(2^m\) closed intervals of
3807: length \(\ell_m\), each containing two intervals of the next stage.  Let
3808: \(\mu\) be the measure giving each of the \(2^m\) intervals of \(F_m\)
3809: mass \(2^{-m}\).  Then \(\mu\) is a nonatomic Borel probability measure
3810: carried by \(F\), and if
3811: \[
3812:  \sum_{m\geq0}2^{-m}\log\frac{1}{\ell_m}=+\infty ,
3813: \]
3814: then \(F\) has vanishing logarithmic capacity, hence is polar.  The
3815: choice \(\ell_0=1\) and \(\ell_m=\rme^{-4^m}\) for \(m\geq1\)
3816: satisfies both hypotheses, since the summands for \(m\geq1\) equal \(2^m\).
3817: \end{lemma}
3818: 
3819: \begin{proof}[Classical, with the divergence check]
3820: The measure \(\mu\) is the weak limit of the normalized Lebesgue measures
3821: on \(F_m\); it is nonatomic because every point of \(F\) lies in nested
3822: intervals of \(\mu\)-mass \(2^{-m}\to0\).  The capacity criterion for
3823: generalized Cantor sets is \cite[p.~31]{Car83}: the set is polar exactly
3824: when the displayed series diverges.  With \(\ell_0=1\) and
3825: \(\ell_m=\rme^{-4^m}\) for \(m\geq1\), one has
3826: \(\ell_1/\ell_0=\rme^{-4}\leq1/2\); for \(m\geq1\),
3827: \(\ell_{m+1}/\ell_m=\rme^{-3\cdot4^m}\leq1/2\) and
3828: \(2^{-m}\log(1/\ell_m)=2^m\), so the series diverges.
3829: \end{proof}
3830: 
3831: \begin{example}[\(\mathcal I\)-equivalent, not \(P\)-equivalent]
3832: \label{ex:ch51-cantor}
3833: Let \(X=\mathbf P^1\) with \(\omega=\ddc\log(1+|z|^2)\), normalized by
3834: \(\int_X\omega=1\), and let \(G_p\) be the Green function of
3835: \Cref{sec:ch51-unit-tests}, so that
3836: \[
3837:  G_p(z)=\log\frac{|z-p|^2}{(1+|z|^2)(1+|p|^2)}\leq0,
3838:  \qquad
3839:  \omega+\ddc G_p=\delta_p .
3840: \]
3841: Let \(F\) and \(\mu\) be as in \Cref{lem:ch51-polar-cantor}, and set
3842: \[
3843:  G_\mu(z):=\int_XG_p(z)\,\rd\mu(p).
3844: \]
3845: 
3846: For \(0\leq s\leq1\), put \(\varphi_s:=sG_\mu\).
3847: 
3848: \emph{The \(\varphi_s\) are genuine potentials.}  Each \(G_p\leq0\), so
3849: \(G_\mu\leq0\).  For \(z\) at chordal distance at least \(\delta\) from
3850: \(F\) one has \(G_p(z)\geq2\log\delta\) for every \(p\in F\), so
3851: \(G_\mu(z)\geq2\log\delta>-\infty\); in particular
3852: \(G_\mu\not\equiv-\infty\).  Fubini gives
3853: \[
3854:  \omega+\ddc G_\mu=\mu ,
3855:  \qquad
3856:  \omega+\ddc\varphi_s=(1-s)\omega+s\mu\ \geq0,
3857: \]
3858: so \(\varphi_s\in\PSH(X,\omega)\) with \(\varphi_s\leq0\).
3859: 
3860: \emph{All Lelong numbers vanish.}  On a Riemann surface every
3861: modification is an isomorphism, so the prime divisors over \(X\) are the
3862: points of \(X\), and
3863: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-three}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lelong:mass}, gives
3864: \[
3865:  \nu(\varphi_s,x)=(\omega+\ddc\varphi_s)(\{x\})
3866:  =(1-s)\omega(\{x\})+s\mu(\{x\})=0
3867: \]
3868: for every \(x\), because \(\omega\) is smooth and \(\mu\) is nonatomic.
3869: By \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3870: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, or directly by Skoda's bound
3871: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lc:smooth}, applied
3872: to \(m\varphi_s\) for every \(m\),
3873: \[
3874:  \mathcal I(m\varphi_s)=\cO_X\quad(m\geq1),
3875:  \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
3876:  \varphi_s\sim_{\mathcal I}0 .
3877: \]
3878: 
3879: \emph{The nonpluripolar mass is \(1-s\).}  The set \(F\) is polar,
3880: hence pluripolar, and \(\mu(F)=1\).  Also \(\omega(F)=0\), since \(F\)
3881: has vanishing Lebesgue measure.  By
3882: \Cref{lem:ch51-npp-bidegree-one} and
3883: \Cref{thm:complex-npp-ledger}, the nonpluripolar product charges no
3884: pluripolar set, so
3885: \[
3886:  \MA_\omega(\varphi_s)
3887:  =\one_{X\setminus F}\bigl((1-s)\omega+s\mu\bigr)
3888:  =(1-s)\omega,
3889:  \qquad
3890:  M_\omega(\varphi_s)=1-s .
3891: \]
3892: The envelope of \(0\) is \(0\), since \(0\) is a competitor and every
3893: competitor is at most zero.  Thus one \(\mathcal I\)-class carries every
3894: mass in \([0,1]\), while
3895: \Cref{cor:ch51-i-canonical-reconstruction} identifies its canonical
3896: normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model representative with \(0\), of mass one.
3897: 
3898: \emph{Conclusion: \(\varphi_{1/2}\not\sim_P0\).}  Both
3899: \(\varphi_{1/2}\) and \(0\)
3900: have positive mass in the K\"ahler class \(\{\omega\}\), so
3901: \Cref{thm:complex-p-projection} applies to both and
3902: \Cref{thm:ch51-hierarchy-strict}, item \cref{itm:ch51-hs:mass}, gives:
3903: if \(\varphi_{1/2}\sim_P0\), then
3904: \(M_\omega(\varphi_{1/2})=M_\omega(0)\), that is \(\tfrac12=1\).  Hence
3905: \[
3906:  \varphi_{1/2}\sim_{\mathcal I}0,
3907:  \qquad
3908:  \varphi_{1/2}\not\sim_P0,
3909:  \qquad
3910:  \varphi_{1/2}\not\sim0 .
3911: \]
3912: Explicitly, \(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) is a model potential with
3913: \(M_\omega(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}])=\tfrac12\) and
3914: \(P_\omega[0]=V_\omega=0\) with mass \(1\), so the two envelopes differ.
3915: Since \(\omega+\ddc P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) has total mass \(1\) and
3916: nonpluripolar mass \(\tfrac12\), it carries mass \(\tfrac12\) on a polar
3917: set; in particular \(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) is unbounded, although all its
3918: Lelong numbers vanish.
3919: 
3920: At the endpoint, \(\varphi_1\) has raw nonpluripolar mass zero but the
3921: same canonical normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model representative \(0\) has
3922: mass one.  Thus neither a raw zero-mass representative nor its raw mass can
3923: be reconstructed from its \(\mathcal I\)-class.
3924: 
3925: \emph{Direction of the failure.}  One implication does survive:
3926: \(\varphi_{1/2}\leq0\) gives \(\varphi_{1/2}\preceq0\), hence
3927: \(\varphi_{1/2}\preceq_P0\).  What fails is the reverse comparison
3928: \(0\preceq_P\varphi_{1/2}\), even though
3929: \(0\preceq_{\mathcal I}\varphi_{1/2}\) holds.
3930: So the second arrow in \eqref{eq:complex-comparison-hierarchy} is not
3931: reversible, and it is not reversible even after restricting to potentials
3932: of positive mass in a K\"ahler class on a curve.
3933: \end{example}"}

3832: \label{ex:ch51-cantor}
3833: Let \(X=\mathbf P^1\) with \(\omega=\ddc\log(1+|z|^2)\), normalized by
3834: \(\int_X\omega=1\), and let \(G_p\) be the Green function of
3835: \Cref{sec:ch51-unit-tests}, so that
3836: \[
3837:  G_p(z)=\log\frac{|z-p|^2}{(1+|z|^2)(1+|p|^2)}\leq0,
3838:  \qquad
3839:  \omega+\ddc G_p=\delta_p .
3840: \]
3841: Let \(F\) and \(\mu\) be as in \Cref{lem:ch51-polar-cantor}, and set
3842: \[
3843:  G_\mu(z):=\int_XG_p(z)\,\rd\mu(p).
3844: \]
3845: 
3846: For \(0\leq s\leq1\), put \(\varphi_s:=sG_\mu\).
3847: 
3848: \emph{The \(\varphi_s\) are genuine potentials.}  Each \(G_p\leq0\), so
3849: \(G_\mu\leq0\).  For \(z\) at chordal distance at least \(\delta\) from
3850: \(F\) one has \(G_p(z)\geq2\log\delta\) for every \(p\in F\), so
3851: \(G_\mu(z)\geq2\log\delta>-\infty\); in particular
3852: \(G_\mu\not\equiv-\infty\).  Fubini gives
3853: \[
3854:  \omega+\ddc G_\mu=\mu ,
3855:  \qquad
3856:  \omega+\ddc\varphi_s=(1-s)\omega+s\mu\ \geq0,
3857: \]
3858: so \(\varphi_s\in\PSH(X,\omega)\) with \(\varphi_s\leq0\).
3859: 
3860: \emph{All Lelong numbers vanish.}  On a Riemann surface every
3861: modification is an isomorphism, so the prime divisors over \(X\) are the
3862: points of \(X\), and
3863: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-three}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lelong:mass}, gives
3864: \[
3865:  \nu(\varphi_s,x)=(\omega+\ddc\varphi_s)(\{x\})
3866:  =(1-s)\omega(\{x\})+s\mu(\{x\})=0
3867: \]
3868: for every \(x\), because \(\omega\) is smooth and \(\mu\) is nonatomic.
3869: By \Cref{thm:complex-strong-openness}, item
3870: \cref{itm:ch51-so:equivalence}, or directly by Skoda's bound
3871: \Cref{prop:ch51-lelong-calculus}, item \cref{itm:ch51-lc:smooth}, applied
3872: to \(m\varphi_s\) for every \(m\),
3873: \[
3874:  \mathcal I(m\varphi_s)=\cO_X\quad(m\geq1),
3875:  \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
3876:  \varphi_s\sim_{\mathcal I}0 .
3877: \]
3878: 
3879: \emph{The nonpluripolar mass is \(1-s\).}  The set \(F\) is polar,
3880: hence pluripolar, and \(\mu(F)=1\).  Also \(\omega(F)=0\), since \(F\)
3881: has vanishing Lebesgue measure.  By
3882: \Cref{lem:ch51-npp-bidegree-one} and
3883: \Cref{thm:complex-npp-ledger}, the nonpluripolar product charges no
3884: pluripolar set, so
3885: \[
3886:  \MA_\omega(\varphi_s)
3887:  =\one_{X\setminus F}\bigl((1-s)\omega+s\mu\bigr)
3888:  =(1-s)\omega,
3889:  \qquad
3890:  M_\omega(\varphi_s)=1-s .
3891: \]
3892: The envelope of \(0\) is \(0\), since \(0\) is a competitor and every
3893: competitor is at most zero.  Thus one \(\mathcal I\)-class carries every
3894: mass in \([0,1]\), while
3895: \Cref{cor:ch51-i-canonical-reconstruction} identifies its canonical
3896: normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model representative with \(0\), of mass one.
3897: 
3898: \emph{Conclusion: \(\varphi_{1/2}\not\sim_P0\).}  Both
3899: \(\varphi_{1/2}\) and \(0\)
3900: have positive mass in the K\"ahler class \(\{\omega\}\), so
3901: \Cref{thm:complex-p-projection} applies to both and
3902: \Cref{thm:ch51-hierarchy-strict}, item \cref{itm:ch51-hs:mass}, gives:
3903: if \(\varphi_{1/2}\sim_P0\), then
3904: \(M_\omega(\varphi_{1/2})=M_\omega(0)\), that is \(\tfrac12=1\).  Hence
3905: \[
3906:  \varphi_{1/2}\sim_{\mathcal I}0,
3907:  \qquad
3908:  \varphi_{1/2}\not\sim_P0,
3909:  \qquad
3910:  \varphi_{1/2}\not\sim0 .
3911: \]
3912: Explicitly, \(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) is a model potential with
3913: \(M_\omega(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}])=\tfrac12\) and
3914: \(P_\omega[0]=V_\omega=0\) with mass \(1\), so the two envelopes differ.
3915: Since \(\omega+\ddc P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) has total mass \(1\) and
3916: nonpluripolar mass \(\tfrac12\), it carries mass \(\tfrac12\) on a polar
3917: set; in particular \(P_\omega[\varphi_{1/2}]\) is unbounded, although all its
3918: Lelong numbers vanish.
3919: 
3920: At the endpoint, \(\varphi_1\) has raw nonpluripolar mass zero but the
3921: same canonical normalized \(\mathcal I\)-model representative \(0\) has
3922: mass one.  Thus neither a raw zero-mass representative nor its raw mass can
3923: be reconstructed from its \(\mathcal I\)-class.
3924: 
3925: \emph{Direction of the failure.}  One implication does survive:
3926: \(\varphi_{1/2}\leq0\) gives \(\varphi_{1/2}\preceq0\), hence
3927: \(\varphi_{1/2}\preceq_P0\).  What fails is the reverse comparison
3928: \(0\preceq_P\varphi_{1/2}\), even though
3929: \(0\preceq_{\mathcal I}\varphi_{1/2}\) holds.
3930: So the second arrow in \eqref{eq:complex-comparison-hierarchy} is not
3931: reversible, and it is not reversible even after restricting to potentials
3932: of positive mass in a K\"ahler class on a curve.
3933: \end{example}

record.search_query: For a plurisubharmonic function pulled back to a model and a prime divisor E, the point Lelong number equals the generic Lelong number along E at a very general point outside a countable union of strict closed analytic subsets.
search_evidence: The theorem search found Siu-type analyticity of Lelong upper-level sets but not the exact very-general-point lemma; the pinned Boucksom text gives the precise result.

source_evidence.comparison: Lines 2171--2174 identify the point Lelong number with the generic Lelong number outside a countable union of strict closed analytic subsets of the divisor, exactly as cited.

record.contextual_definition_comparison: The generic Lelong number along E is the infimum of point Lelong numbers on E and is attained at very general points. Taking the union of the exceptional sets for the countable sequence u_j and U remains countable.
record.applicability: For each fixed prime divisor E, the divisor cannot be covered by the countable union of its strict analytic subsets, so one point works simultaneously for all u_j and U. No uniform point across different E is needed.
record.detail: The proof uses precisely the countable simultaneous selection licensed by Lemma 10.5.

record.location: Proof, maximum/envelope and multiplier-ideal paragraphs: Boucksom Corollary 10.18 and its approximation interface
record.search_query: For a plurisubharmonic weight phi on a smooth complex manifold, a holomorphic function f belongs to the multiplier ideal J(phi) if and only if there exists epsilon>0 such that ord_E(f) is at least (1+epsilon)nu_E(phi)-A_X(E) for every prime divisor E over X.
search_evidence: The theorem search returned definitions and related multiplier-ideal results but not the exact global valuative iff; the fixed Boucksom source contains Corollary 10.18 with the stated quantifiers.

source_evidence.comparison: Lines 2369--2370 state Corollary 10.18: membership in J(phi) is equivalent to one epsilon>0 satisfying the discrepancy inequality for all prime divisors over X. Equal divisorial profiles therefore give identical membership tests at every integral scaling.

Lines 2336--2341 record the analytic multiplier-ideal approximants and the exact discrepancy error nu_E(phi)-A_X(E)/k <= nu_E(phi_k) <= nu_E(phi), matching the source interface used to recover divisorial Lelong numbers from the full ideal tower.

record.contextual_definition_comparison: The proof and source use prime divisors on all smooth modifications and log discrepancy A_X(E). The release-local Chapter 51 normalization rescales Lelong and multiplier weights together and explicitly verifies that the criterion determines I(lambda phi) for every lambda>0.
record.applicability: The proof compares equal divisorial profiles, so the exact same uniform-epsilon membership predicate holds for every local holomorphic function at every positive integral scaling. Conversely, the full tower determines the profile via the approximation bound. This justifies both maximum closure and [U]_I=d.
record.detail: The iff direction, single uniform epsilon, discrepancy term, all-divisor quantifier, scaling, and tower/profile equivalence are all preserved.
